Its appointed duration is three years. The deity is the Goddess Śrī. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Śrī!”. [I take] leave. Its result is your face being beautiful and calm, being rich in rice, many people will love you and have sympathy for you.

There is the observance of not chewing betel. Its appointed duration is one year, and one month. The deity is the Reverend Manodeva I have choosen the word manodeva attested in ms. M and N, rather than aśvino attested in ms. G; asvido attested in ms. P; and maṣnodeva attested in ms. U because the word manodeva is quite similar to Manobhava as the god of love (see OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is probably similar to the localisation of the god Manobhu in the context of Bali. The word manodeva is also appropriate to the dative mantra manodevāya when compared to the others in this passage. Another important reason is that the result of this observance is meṅət rūpanta manis, mvaṅ akveh bhrānta hyun iri kita: ‘your face will be sweet and deeply loved, and many people will fall in love with you.’ This result of the observance is strongly related to the Manobhava as mentioned in 3.10 riṅ rūpa tan pasiriṅ, akveh rәsəp asih iri kita, and 3.203 pinakarūpa, aśrī sumilah.. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Manodeva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your face will be sweet [and] deeply loved, and many people will be sick with love for you

There is the observance of ‘Easy Breath’ Another alternative translation of Lәga Prāṇa is ‘Contented Life’. Literally, the word lәga means ‘open, satisfied, content, relieved; taking lightly, accepting, renouncing readily’ (OJED s.v.), and the word prāṇa means ‘1. breath; first of the five vital airs (see pañcabāyu); 2. the breath of life, life; 3. (as a seat of the feelings:) heart, soul; 4. the place on the body where one can be mortally wounded (where one's life is located), esp. the breast; mortal (of a wound); 5. numeral coefficient for living creatures’ (OJED s.v.). (Lәga Prāṇa): if one eats carrying a kris on his lap. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The mantra is: “Om hail to Rudra!” [I take] leave. Its result is that many people will be ready to sacrifice their lives for your life; many people will be compassionate and will love you.

There is the observance of ‘Hero’I assume that the word bīra here is the other form of vīra which is refers to brave man, hero, valiant warrior; brave, valiant (OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is often in Old Javanese, for instance the word bulan ‘moon’ also has other form as vulan. (Bīra): if one eats salt as meat. Its appointed duration is one year and three months. The deity is the Lord Iśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Īśvara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that all your efforts will be achieved quickly; you will be loved by mankind, and the Gods [and] the Demons will love you.

There is the observance of not eating the betel leaf [rubbed] by lime. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Goddess Bhagāvati. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Bhagāvati!” [I take] leave. Its result is being free from all poisons; there will be no obstacle upon you.

There is the observance of eating the leaves on which food is served. Its appointed duration is seven years. The deity is the Lord Īśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Īśvara” An interesting textual phenomenon can be observed here. The mss. M, N and U contain the mantra: om̐ mam̐ īśvarāya namaḥ, whereas G contains the mantra: mantra kadi ṅuni, meaning ‘the mantra is as before’. This phenomenon goes beyond lexical synonymy, but is a synonym in syntax scope. The ms. G refers to a previous mantra that already exists in the initial passage (4v-5r), which contains om̐ mam̐ iśvarāya namaḥ.. [I take] leave. Its result is to reach the heaven of Lord Īśvara. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a clothes vendorI have chosen the word basana in ms. G instead of the word bhāṣa in M N U because of the parallel with the MM in passage 5 (hana brata akarvan patrāhāra ṅaranya, pituṅ tahun samayanya, ⟨phalanya⟩ mulih mariṅ svarga saṅ hyaṅ iśvara, sasarnya ajanma riṅ juru basana, sugih hulun, labdha ri saṅ prabhu.). The word basana was derived from the Sanskrit word vasana ‘clothes, garment, attire’ (see OJED, s.v.). , rich in servants, successful with the king and his minister, [and] you will not be unsurpassed by all your companionsLexically, the sentence tan pada lavan rovaṅta kabeh can be translated as ‘you will not be equal to all your companions’. I translated this sentence more liberal as ‘unsurpassed by all your companions’. .

There is the observance of ‘Eating Fruit (especially edible roots and fruits)’ (Ṅraka) I have chosen the word ṅraka as attested in mss. M N and U as a kind of a vernacular form of Old Javanese in Bali which is not attested in OJED. However, the meaning is the same with the word araka which means ‘taking, seizing, robbing, food (esp. edible roots and fruit?)' as attested in ms. G. : one eats every kind of fruit. Its appointed duration is three years. Its deity is the Reverend Īśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ mam̐ hail to Śiva!” Mss. M P and U contains the mantra: om̐ mam̐ ⟨śivā⟩ya namaḥ svāhā, whereas the ms. G contains mantra kadi ṅūni. See my footnote in passage 3.16. [I take] leave. Its result is reaching the abode of the Lord Śiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a wise priest, rich in silver, successful with the king and ministers.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Kumbhakarṇa’ (Aṅumbhakarṇa)This observance is interesting because it imitates the behavior of Kumbhakarṇa as a young brother of Rāvāṇa in the Rāmāyaṇa epic. On the basis of Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa, the figure of Kumbhakarṇa is always sleeping. However he woke up when he heard the quintessence speech of his grandfather. The Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa mentions the figure of Kumbhakarṇa as follows: Kāla saṅ kaki sәḍәṅ mavara-varah, Kumbhakarṇa sira jagra ya rumәṅə̄, de nikari ujar-ujar pasili-silih, śīghra yar pavuṅu arddha varurutәn ‘when his grandfather was giving his admonishment, Kumbhakarṇa woke up, and on hearing the conversation quickly became attentive, though still very sleepy’ (see Santoso, 1980: 358).: when one sleeps on one side [position] for one year, lies on the back face up for one year, [then] lies face downwards for one year. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity of the observance is the Lord Rudra. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Rudra!” [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be loved by the learned men; all humans will respect you; all your aims will be successful.

Furthermore, if one is silent when defecating, the desire I have translated the word prih as ‘desire’, as this is its meaning in Balinese (KBI, 2016: 730). OJED (s.v.) defines the word prih as ‘effort, exertion, full attention, great care and devotion’. is achieved quickly, [and] you will have many disciples.
And, if you are silent when sweeping, the result is that you will be loved by the learned man as well as gods and rulers; [your] reincarnation will be good.
And, if you are silent when polishing teeth, the result is that your purpose will be achieved.
And, if one is silent when applying the [holy] ash (bhasma), the result is that one reaches the abode of the Goddess Rātri. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a learned man.

There is the observance of not using the mat when one sleeps. Its appointed duration is one year and three months. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Nāga-King. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the Nāga-King!” [I take] leave. Its result is that gods and demons will love you; and you will obtain all the good qualities.

There is the observance of sleeping in a leaning position. Its appointed duration is three months. The deity is the Lord Viṣṇu. The mantra is: “Om̐ Um̐ I have chosen the bīja-akṣara Um̐, as attested in G, rather than Om̐ in M, N and U, because the deity being worshipped in this passage is Viṣṇu. According to Tantraśāstra (Kumar Rai, 1978), the bīja-akṣara U often denotes Viṣṇu, as well as Śiva, Pranava, Daksakarna, and Amaresvara. hail to Viṣṇu!”. [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be magically effective at speaking to all mankind, [and] will receive gifts.

There is the observance of ‘Life’ (Prāṇa): one does not eat anything that breaths, namely any living beings. Its appointed duration is seven years. The deity is the Reverend Devātara. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Devātara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that you will have many children, livestock, buffalo and ox; every kind of plant that is planted by you will grow.

There is the observance of eating once a day. Its deity is the Reverend Śambhu. Its appointed duration is one year. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Śambhu!” [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be reborn as the son of a noble family; you will be famous, and all your aims, whatever [they are], will be fulfilled; your desire will be met quickly.

There is the observance of eating once a day. The deity of the observance is Reverend Śambhu. Its appointed duration is three years. Its result is that you will be rich in offspring See OJED s.v. drәman, ‘prosperous, thriving, rich (in children), happy, privileged, of exemplary conduct’. ; all your desires will be fulfilled quickly.

There is the observance of eating once a day, [according to] all your abilitiesSakavaśa could be analysed as being formed by the prefix sa- + kavaśa 1. (ka-pass., cf vinaśa) ‘overpowered, dominated, mastered, subdued, in the power (of)’, but the meaning that is intended here is closer to the active forms aṅavaśa, kumavaśa, paṅavaśa, ‘(avs) to be powerful, have an inescapable force, overpowering, dominating; to force os., make bold, struggle to attain’. Compare vaśa, baśa, ‘1. (Skt) power, force, dominion’. In this context, I assume that kavaśa corresponds to the Balinese kavasa = kuasa ‘in a position of authority, (to have the) right, etc.’ (KBI 2016: 684) plus sa-, which here I freely translate ‘according to your abilities to…’ to perform the observance. The deity is the Reverend Śambhu. Its result is that you will be reborn as the son of a noble family, [and] all your aims will be achieved.

There is an observance when one eats following the moonlight (Anūtakәn Vulan). The technical details are as follows. On the first day after the waxing moon, [you eat only] a handful. If the waxing period of the moon increases, it [should be] added by a handful until fifteen handfuls when the full moon, because it adds a handful every day. However, on the waning moon, it should decrease by a handful every day. Finally, one fasts during the dark moon. Its appointed duration is three months. The deity is the Lord Indra. Mantra: “Om̐ salutations to god Indra!” [I take] leave.
Its result is to reach the heaven of the Lord Śiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a smart king, and a priest who has many disciples.

There is the observance of ‘Eating Leaves’ (Pattrāhāra): one eats leaves continuously. Its deity is Lord Maheśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ Om̐ hail to Maheśvara!”. [I take] leave. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Guru. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one reaches the heaven of the Lord Brahmā, and the Lord Viṣnu in the future.

There is the observance of ‘Eating Fruit’ (Phalāhāra): one eats every kind of fruit continuously. Its deity is the Lord Brahmā. The mantra is: “Om̐ Am̐ hail to Brahmā!” [I take] leave. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Guru, and obtaining the abode of Śiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a son of a noble family in the future.

There is the observance of ‘Not Smelling’ (Nirambə̄): one does not eat any kind [of food] with smell. Its deity is the Lord Rudra. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Rudra!” [I take] leave. Its result is reaching the abode of the Lord Rudra. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a beautiful and wise [person].

There is the observance of ‘Every Ninth Month’ (Ṅasaṅa): one fasts on every the ninth month (Kasaṅa). The deity is the Reverend Bāyu. The mantra is: “Om̐ Tam̐ hail to Bāyu!” [I take] leave. Its result is to reach the heaven of the Lord Prajāpati; [you will] experience happiness from childhood into old age.

There is the observance of fasting every twelve days in the bright half of the lunar month on the seventh month (Kapitu). It is called the observance of the Lord Bhīma. The mantra is: “Om̐ Bam̐ hail to Bhīma!” [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be a brave man [and] trusted by the king, rich in gold and silver, and young servants; you will have many children; your activity will be successful.

There is the observance of ‘holding in one’s hands’ (Aṅasta): one eats on a vessel While the word haryan means ‘II banana-leaf; a leaf on which food is served (in the following examples there is much that is uncertain)’ (OJED s.v.), here I take it to refer more generally to the vessel – usually a leaf, indeed – on which food is served. The image is thus that the practitioner should use his hand instead of the leaf to eat food. See the use of the word taṅan ‘hand’ instead of ‘leaf’ in the clause tumpaṅakәn iṅ taṅan, ‘The food is to be formed like a rice cone on the hand’. Apparently, the practitioner should put salt in the lowest layer and then the other food above it, without salt. [that is] the palm of the left hand The word haryan means ‘banana-leaf; a leaf on which food is served (in the following examples there is much that is uncertain)’ (OJED: 599:5). Furthermore, the word lĕpa-lĕpa, lĕlĕpa palm of the hand or sole of the foot (OJED: 1011:8.1). Because both words have quite similar meanings, that is why I translated it as on the palm of the left hand. In this context, the author seems to associate the haryan ‘leaf’ and ‘lәpa-lәpa’ just like ‘plate’. salt as meat. It is to be formed like a rice cone on the hand. It would be better without salt. Its result is that your supernatural power [will be] great; your intelligence [will be] firm, without any mental disturbance.

There is the observance of ‘Sleeping in the First Lunar Fortnight’ (Pratipāda Supta): if one sleeps once [during the day], one is not [supposed] to sleep again. Its result is that the [black] magic will fear you.

There is the observance of ‘the Junction of the Three Divisions of the Day’ (Trisandhyā): one takes a bath three times a day, including at night. Its result is that one will be beautiful; he will be rich [and] superior because of religious austerity Here the expression lәvih sakiṅ tapa could also be translated ‘superior to an ascetic’. —that is its outcome.

There is the observance of the ‘a Favorable Day’ (Amr̥tamāsa): one uses the leaf of a vuṅlon (Nephelium Lappaceum) as a vessel [for eating], and especially its fruit as a hollow bowl. Its result is that all your activities will be successful, [and] you will be beautiful, rich and famous.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Irrigated Rice-Field’ (Navahan) I have conjectured the word narahan, as attested in the mss. G, M, N and U, to navahan. The word navahan is derived from N- + savah + -an, meaning ‘behaving like an irrigated rice field’. This is also supported by the technique used for the observance: one does not eat anything that grows from Śrī, the goddess of rice and crops. : one does not eat anything that grows from Śrī (the goddess of rice/crops). [However,] you can eat all kinds of flesh. Its result is that all your activities will be successful; you will be desired by women.

There is the observance of the ‘Fleshless’ (Nirāmiṣa): one does not eat any kinds of flesh, like: water-buffalo (carabeef), ox (beef), and pig (pork). As the foremost thing that you should not eat is just any kind of [flesh] that cannot be cooked. Fish is what you should eat: [fish] that live in rivers and ponds, that live in the sea, and corals. These you can eat. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that you are superior to all [other] men ; there is no one who will be equal to you; and you reach the heaven of the Lord Viṣṇu. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one will be reborn as a priest who has many disciples. It is very good.

There is the observance of the ‘Fleshless’ (Nirāmiṣa): if one eats salt as meat. Its appointed duration is three years. Its deity is the Reverend Iśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Īśvara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that all your desires are achieved quickly, and you will be loved by mankind, and Gods and demons [will] love you.

There is the observance of ‘The Wick of the Moon’ (Candravr̥tti) I suspect that the variation between candravr̥ti and cakravartti in the title of this brata stems from the fact that both candra ‘moon’ and cakra ‘wheel’ are round in shape.I chose to use candravṛti as the name of this brata because it aligns with the technical description of the practice, which explains that one makes a moon shape (candra rūpa) by burning cooked rice in the shape and size of a monkey’s head.:
one makes a moon shape by burning cooked rice in the shape and size of a monkey’s head. When you are eating, the wick is lit by placing it on the cooked rice moulded into the shape of a monkey's head. You should face east while eating. If the wick goes out, you should stop eating. The result is that whatever you do will come quickly, whatever you strive for will be obtained, and you [will] become famous and loved by learned men and the king. Everyone [will] love [you] and be pleased.

There is the observance of ‘Being Red’ (Ṅrakta): one eats glutinous red [rice]. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is that whatever you do is successful, and [you will] reach the heaven of the Lord Brahmā. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a rich merchant.

There is the observance of ‘Difficulty’ (Durga): one eats the cooked rice mixed with finger millet. Its appointed duration is five months. Its result is reaching the heaven of the reverend Viṣṇu. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a priest who has many disciples.

There is the observance of the ‘Golden Ladle’ (Kaṇakadrava): one eats yellow rice. Its appointed duration is three years. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Reverend Mahādeva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a rich ship captain.

There is the observance of the ‘Eating the Fruit’ (Phalāhāra): one eats every kind of fruit. Its appointed duration is three months. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Sadāśiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a rich person, with many disciples, and many followers.

There is the observance of ‘Smoking [Food]’ (Ndhūma): one does not eat [food] that is touched by fire. Its appointed duration is three years. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Brahmā. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a rich person since childhood, [and] perfectly beautiful.

There is the observance of ‘[fasting on every] Kalivon [day]’ (Ṅalivon)This passage does not provide a detailed explanation of the technique for performing the observance. I assume that the word mopavāsa ‘fasting’ is needed here to complete the explanation. The word brata itself also has the meaning of a ‘holy practice’ (fasting, continence, etc.): one should carry it out [for] seven Kalivon-Saturdays. Its result is that [one’s] desires are achieved quickly.

There is the observance of eating all kinds of seeds (Sarvavīja), and the tip of alaṅ-alaṅ (Imperata cylindrica) grass. Its result is that you will be ‘thunder-voiced’, have powerful mantras, and be victorious.

There is the observance of ‘Earth Plate’ I translated bhūmipattra as ‘earth plate’, not ‘earth leaf’, to indicate the practice of brata, which involves using the earth or soil as a dining plate. I suspect that practitioners of this brata would place their food directly on the ground. (Bhūmipāttra): if one eats without using plates. Its appointed duration is nine years. Its result is that learned men will be kindly disposed towards [you], [you will be] rich in land and freeholds; your relatives and kinsmen are prosperous, [you] are trusted by mankind, [have] many disciples, are [knowledgeable in] sciences and sacred doctrines, [you] are treated with respect by the king; your yoga is just like the sitting posture of the Gaṇa Regarding the technique of performing the brata that involves placing food directly on the ground, I am more inclined to translate the yoga of śila gaṇa as “your yoga is just like the sitting posture of the Gaṇa”. This is supported by passage 3.314 of this text, which also uses the word yoga to refer to a sitting posture. In the brata called nūtakәn Saśila Bhaṭāra Gaṇa—‘following all the conduct of Lord Gaṇa’ — there is a specific gesture that follow the behavior of Bhaṭāra Gaṇa with the phrase tiṅkahiṅ amaṅan, śīla gaṇa ‘The manner is to sit politely on the ground with the legs crossed, as the Gaṇa’s position while eating’. I realize that the technique for performing the brata in this passage seems to have been transposed because it appears in the section explaining the results of performing the brata. Therefore, another alternative translation for the yoganya śila gaṇa is ‘you are fit and possess many qualities’. This expression is found in the Khmer dictionary, where it means ‘you are fit and possess many qualities’ or ‘having many virtues’.For a more detailed discussion of yoga and meditation in the context of Old Javanese and Balinese traditions, please read Acri’s (2021) article titled Yoga and Meditation Traditions in Insular Southeast Asia'. . Such is its result.

There is the observance of following the flowers of the Lord Gaṇa: one should succeed eating six handfuls [of food] every day. Its result is reaching the abode of the Lord Guru. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a green ascetic (viku hijo) A detailed explanation of the viku hijo ‘green monk’ can be found in the Tantu Panggәlaran. In that text, it is explained that a viku ijo is an unmarried monk. When he sought ordination from Bhaṭāra Guru, he was not given a siṅhәl (headdress) made of daluvaṅ (bark paper), but was given a siṅhәl of the leaves of alang-alang grass. That is why he is called viku hijo ‘green monk’ (hana taruṇa anvam ... ya ta iṅaskara de bhaṭāra Guru tan siniṅĕlan ta ya daluvaṅ, siniṅĕlan ta ya rvan iṅ halalaṅ, tinĕhĕr viku hijo ṅaranya) (Robson and Sidomulyo, 2021: 37)., having the supernatural power of being able to see from afar; [further,] whatever one says it is obeyed.
There is the observance of not drinking water after eating. Its appointed duration is seven years. Its result is that your merit is not lost.

There is the observance of not drinking water, [and] chewing betel without turning [its leaf upside down]. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is one [will be] fitted with a loincloth by a woman. If one is a woman, she [will be] covered with tapihTapih is a garment worn by women around the lower part of the body (= siñjaṅ) (OJED, s.v.). by a man The expressions cinavetan dening strī, meaning ‘fitted with a loincloth by a woman’, and yaniṅ strī tinapihan dening kakuṅ, meaning ‘if one is a woman, she will be covered with tapih by a man’, probably refer to spouses who respect each other.. And then, the poison will not be effective upon you.

There is the observance of ‘Following the Eleventh Day’ (Ṅekadaśi): on the eleventh day of the waxing moon in the tenth month (kasapuluh) you are fasting. It should be performed for three consecutive tenth months. Its result is reaching the abode of the Lord Īśvara. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a powerful king.

There is the observance which is superior to the five silences (pañca mona) According to the Tattva Brata as transmitted in Javanese tradition no 56, we know that the pañcamona consist of five types of silent, namely the observance of being silent while eating (mona maṅan), being silent while sweeping (mona nanapuh), being silent when applying the holy ash (mona bhasma), being silent while chewing (mona susur), and being silent when defecating (mona ṅisiṅ). , namely to be silent at all times, which coversThe word aṅraṅkul means ‘1: raṅkul 1508:6 aṅraṅkul, rumaṅkul, rinaṅkul 1508:6.1 to embrace, seize with the arms, hold in a grip’ (OJED s.v.). In this context I decided to choose the word ‘cover’ for a more liberal translation. all [other] observances. Its results are finding great happiness, being reborn as a rich person from childhood, being rich in cooked rice, and then all your words will be obeyed by all mankind.
There is the observance of ‘Steaming Rice’ (Maḍaṅ): one does not eat steamed rice. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that many people are pleased with you.
There is the observance of not taking a bath, and not applying oil. Its appointed duration is three months. Its result is that one becomes perfect in beauty, wise, [and one] is loved by all people.

There is the observance of not being difficult [with food] I have chosen the tan pinakevuhan ‘not being difficult’, as attested in ms. M and N, rather than kinimbuhan ‘not being added’ in P, and pakevuhan ‘not difficult’ in manuscript U, as this is consistent with the technical explanation of brata in the subsequent part of this passage, namely tan karәṇan ‘not being attracted’. I assume this passage is closely related to the brata sarvabhakṣa ‘eating or devouring everything’. However, the variation found in P, tan kinimbuhan ‘not being added’, is quite important to consider as an alternative of this observance in this passage. , not being attracted [by food], [and] not being allowed to eat together [with other people]. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is being obeyed by mankind, [and being] perfect in beauty; [any] desire is achieved quickly.
There is the observance of eating without [adding] additional [food besides a single portion]. Its appointed duration is seven years. Its result is that any desire is achieved quickly.

There is the observance of ‘Every Sunday’ (Aṅraditya): one fasts every Sunday. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is having a speech like thunderbolt, having a powerful mantra, [and] you will be winning over enemies.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Pāṇḍava’ (Maṇḍava): one eats five handfuls [of food] daily. Its appointed duration is five months. Its results are possessing the eight preternatural qualities [of a yogin], [and becoming] perfectly famous.

There is the observance of ‘[Behaving like] Saṅ Bhīma’ (Saṅ Bhīma): one fasts on the fourteenth day of the waxing moon in the seventh moon (Kapitu). Its result is having abundant happiness, having a powerful mantra, winning over enemies, being obeyed by mankind, being knowledgeable and skillful in playing gamәlan, [and] singing, being rich in gold and silver, and in servants, livestock, buffalos, [and] oxen, having many estates. The right way of performing this is: in the middle of the night you are standing up on one leg, not sleeping, and !promising! You will be successful.

There is the observance of not eating pork. Its result is that you are unaffected by all kinds of poisons, and skin diseases [like] leprosy, and all of them will be drifted away, you will have powerful mantras; all Gods, demons, learned man and humans will love [you].

There is the observance of ‘Cutting Off the Taste’ (Mәgat Rasa)This observance shares the same name as passage 3.1, but the technique and result are different.: one does not eat pork, does not eat [the meat of animals] with fangs; does not eat the taṅiri-fish; does not eat greasy glutinous rice; does not eat durian (Durio zibethinus), as well as jackfruit, reddish banana; does not eat green peas; or tuber and hanging fruits. Its result is that [you will have] excellent supernatural power; all your wishes [will be] fulfilled quickly.

There is the observance of ‘Every Tenth Month’ (April-May) (Ṅasapuluh): it is the observance of the reverend one who is worshiped in temple-grounds (Saṅ Sinuhun iṅ Panataran). The right way of performing this is: one drinks water without chewing betel. It should be started on the first day of the waxing moon in the tenth month. It should be finished on the dark moon of the tenth month. Its appointed duration is one month.
One arranges the offerings prior to beginning [the observance]. When undertaking the observance, one will be worshipping at the shrine. The offerings [include]: rice cone with a pleasantly rich taste (tumpәṅ gurih), [and] meat of a wild duck (ivak aṅlambara itik). It should be accompanied by small dried salty fish (gәraṅ gәrih), crab [meat], eggs, bean-sprouts, boiled pelasPelas are complementary offerings such as small pepes made from keluak. , salty shrimps, banana flowers, edible roots and fruit, young coconut, sugar-cane, water from a spring (bañu kuvuṅ), colourful flowers, fragrant flowers that are garlanded, colourful lotuses, campaka-flowers (Michelia campaka), every kind of fragrant flower. These should [also] be offered to God: colourful lotuses, fragrant sesame oil, fragrant cosmetic unguent, a cosmetic unguent or lotion of sweets and dainties, every kind of tidbit, a set of white garments. The complete payment [for the performing of the ceremony] is money [amounting to]: 225, [plus] incense, lamp, mәñanBenzoin or gum benjamin, a (red) resin used for incense and obtained from the Styrax benzoin (OJED, s.v.). , sandalwood, sandalwood powder, grains, flowers, [and] flowers for scattering [as part of religious observances].
This is the way [of] reciting the mantra: one should begin with offering sasәḍәpFinely chopped betel etc with dadap leaves, bras and kuñit used as basma on the temples, between the eyes, on the head and the shoulder-blades (esp. in certain ceremonies). In añәñәḍĕp the name-giving ceremony seems to be meant (OJED, s.v.). . Kavrәtta mixed with honey should be used as sasәḍәpSee footnote above.. When beginning [the actual ritual], one should offer fragrance (kavaṅi) at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the illustrious Mahādeva!”
After presenting the offerings, the mantra is: “Om̐, I arrange the Himalayan cedar, Sa Ba Ta A I, hail to Śiva, A U ma, Ah! Om̐, may the Gods be happy!.”
After scattering the flowers, one should perform the observance through drinkingThe anәkul means ‘eating the cooked rice’ (OJED, s.v.). In this context, I have translated it as ‘drinking’ because it is followed by the word bañu which means ‘water’. One can interpret the anәkul bañu as ‘the activity in eating the water of the cooked rice’. water for one month [and] stop [drinking it] in the dark moon. Such sәsәḍәp is salt mixed with charcoal. The mantra is: ‘Om̐ hail to the Mahādeva, hail! Hail to Śiva! May there be no obstacle.
The offering when finishing the observance are various bowls of rice with flowers as their meat. The mantra is just like before. When concentrating on the offering, [the mantra] is just like when one begins it. [After] coming to an end, the mantra is ‘Om̐’.

There is the observance of the ‘Cow-Bearer’ (Godhara)This is my conjecture from the word kodara in mss. N and M, which do not yield any appropriate meanings. I have chosen the word godhara derived from go meaning ‘cow’ (OJED, s.v.) and dhara meaning ‘bearing’ (OJED, s.v.), as these make sense in the context of performing the observance. The practitioner who wants to perform this observance should abstain from killing, eating living creatures, and violence (ahimsa), as these are all associated with the cow. Furthermore, the clothes worn during this observance should be a white garment and a turmeric-coloured bracelet on the right hand, which are strongly linked with the appearance of the cow.. Its appointed duration is one month. It should begin on the first day of the waxing moon in the second month (August-September). One should not eat any living creatures and any kind [of creatures] that come from the ocean. You [should] have a tranquil appearance by wearing a white garment, and by wearing a bracelet that is coloured with turmeric in the right hand. Do not commit the crime of killing any kind of living creatures.

As for the offering to begin the observance, it is cooked rice on the tamas Tamas is a serving tray made of young palm fronds, round in shape (KBI, 2016: 966.) . It should be [completed] by all kinds of vegetables as its meat in the limasLimas is a kind of offering vessels made of palm fronds shaped like pyramids, used to hold nuts (KBI, 2016: 582).: every kind of eggplant (tuvuṅ), bitter melon (papare), bael (baligo), hot condiment (sambal), all of them without shrimp paste (tarasi); fried moringa fruit (kәlentaṅ), fried cacaṅanonIn the context of Hindu ceremonial practices in Bali, cacaṅanon or cacaṅon refers to the accompanying items in an offering (bantәn), such as sugarcane, bananas, cushions, tape, and jajan gina/uli. These components are arranged to symbolize the philosophical concepts of fertility and offering (source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pDdReMERGb0=12s). , and fried creeper with bitter fruits. All of these are wrapped in black mustard (sasavi), [and one scatters] fried onions starting from the north [to the other directions]. After cooking, one lays the offerings on the cooked rice in the tamas. Especially if there is milk, [and] oil, [they should be put] in the container of limas. One should beautifully arrange a variety of fruits, whole banana flowers, young coconut, ritual substances [like] incense, lamps, [and] sandalwood powder.
All the offerings should be made ready for the Lord Gaṇapati, the reverend Bhr̥ṅgiriṭi, the Reverend Īśvara, [and] the Goddess Umā. The offerings should be offered to all of them.

You should start performing the observance by purifying and cleansing [your] body. [After that] you should worship at the shrine. The mantra is: ‘Om̐, hail to Nandīśvara and Mahākāla!’ ‘Om̐, hail to the Bhṛṅgiriṭis!’ ‘Om̐, hail to the Seven Sages!’ ‘Om̐, hail to Maheśvara!’ ‘Om̐, hail to the illustrious Umā!’ After that, present your offerings to God. The mantra is: ‘Om̐ hail to Iṁ!’ ‘Om̐ hail to divine Caru!’ To the one whose essence is immortality, Svāhā!’.

At the end, you should carry out the observance again in the same way as before, [when you started it]. The yellow thread bracelet should be removed [from your hand]. You should finalize [the observance] only on the dark moon of the Bhadravāda (August-September).

This is the way of performing the observance on a favorable day (Amṛtamāsa). You should start by completely extinguishing the fire for one day. The offerings consist of all kinds of pure [foods]: white rice cones, roasted duck, small dried salted fish, eggs, betel leaves and areca nuts (pinang), edible roots and fruits, banana flower, [and a] complete [set of] aromatics A complete set of incense aromatics is typically made of sandalwood, frankincense, agarwood, and other materials. .The following are [the details of the rites], one by one:

In the fourth month (October-November), on the full moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Moon [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the day of the full moon. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the lunar world.” Your offerings [should be made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for the God. Hail to the Moon God!”

In the fifth month (November-December), on the dark moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Maitri [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the day of the dark moon. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to Agni world.” Your offerings [should be made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Agni God!”

In the sixth month (December-January), on the eighth day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Kr̥ṣṇa [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the eighth day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Viṣṇu world.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Viṣṇu God!”

In the seventh month (January-February), on the thirteenth day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Baruna [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the thirteenth day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Rudra world.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Rudra God!”

In the eighth month (February-March), on the second day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Vivasvan [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the second day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Sun world.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Sūrya god!”

In the ninth month (March-April), on the sixth day of the waxing month, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Amśuman [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on this sixth day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Arka world.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Arka God!”

In the tenth month (April-May), on the fourth day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐, Dhatr̥ [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the fourth day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Brahmā world.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Dhatṛ!”

In the eleventh month (May-June), on the fifth day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Indra [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the fifth day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Indra heaven.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Indra God!”

In the twelfth month (June-July), on the first day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Aryaman [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the first day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Arka world.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offerings for God. Hail to the Arka God!”

In the first month (July-August), on the tenth day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐, Bhagha I have emended the word bhaghana to bhaga because I could not find a proper definition of bhaghana in the MWSD or the OJED. In this context, the word bhaga is really appropriate because it refers to another name of Āditya, as mentioned at the end of this mantra: sūryalokam sa gacchati, meaning ‘one goes to the world of Sūrya. Monier Williams explains the word bhaga as bestowing wealth and presiding over love and marriage; brother of the Dawn; regent of the Nakṣatra Uttara-Phalgunī’. Yāska also lists him among the highest-sphere divinities. According to a later legend, Rudra destroyed his eyes (MWSD s.v.).[grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the tenth dayI have emended daśimyun tu to daśami as a feminin (strī liṅga) in gender and locative (saptamī vibhakti) . Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Bhaga world.” Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the offering for God. Hail to the Bhaga God!”

In the second month (August-September), on the seventh day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: Om̐ Pūṣan [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the seventh day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Sūrya world. Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐, hail to the offering for God. Hail to the Pūṣan!”

In the third month (September-October), on the ninth day of the waxing moon, the praise [of the god should take place] at the shrine. The mantra is: “Om̐ Parjanya [grant] the immortality of the gods. Let there be praise for you on the seventh day. Deliver me from all sins. One goes to the Indra world. Your offerings should be [made in the same way] as before. The mantra is: “Om̐, hail to the offering for God. Hail to the Indra!”

The way of performing the observance has been completed. On a favourable day (Amṛtamāsa), one should extinguish the fire of the twelve months. The one who performs the observance will obtain a completely long life in the future, [and] be reborn as a supreme king. Do not tell others indiscriminately when performing the observance. It is finished!

It is also very auspicious to perform the observance on the day before [full moon or dark moon] and on any day leading up to them]. Whenever you always perform the observance, it ensure that the soul of your ancestor will be rejois, up to your grandfathers and great-grandfathers will be happy. It is also make their soul be happy. This is the blessing that nourishes one's body and soul.

There is the observance of ‘The Bath of Encompassing the World’ (Adyus Anuṅku Rāt) Adyus Anuṅku Rāt literally means ‘The Bath of Encompassing the World’. Within the context of this text, the term ‘encompassing the world’ refers to a specific temporal dimension, wherein a spiritual practitioner performs the ritual purification bath every month throughout the full twelve-month cycle of a year without interruption.All explanations relating to the dauh can be found in KBI (2016: 224).:

In the month of Śrāvaṇa (July-August), one takes a bathThere is a tendency in mss. M and N to treat the word adyus with the addition of the suffix irrealis -a, making it adyusa in the performance of this monthly brata. If this tendency is followed, the translation becomes ‘one should take a bath’. once in the afternoon, at around 3.00 pm - 4.30 pm. Its result is that the servant will love you.
In the month of Bhādravada (August-September), one takes a bath at around 10.30 am – 12.00 am. Its result is being renown that fills the world.
In the month of Asuji (September-October), one takes a bath at around 12.00 pm – 01.30 pm. Its result is that all kinds of silver comes.
In the month of Kārttika (October-November), one takes a bath at around 04.30 pm – 06.00 pm at night. Its result is being rich in offspring.
In the month of Mārgaśira (November-December), one takes a bath at around 10.30 pm –12:00 pm at night. Its result is being loved by the king.
In the month of Poṣya (December-January), one takes a bath at around 01.30 pm – 03.00 pm. Its result is being a brave man.
In the month of Māgha (January-February), one takes a bath [and] wakes up at around 04.30 pm – 06.00 pm. Its result is being rich in paddy.
In the month of Phalguṇa (February-March), one takes a bath at around 07.30 am – 09.00 am at daylight. Its result is that a large amount of food is obtained.
In the month of Cetra (March-April), one takes a bath at around 09.00 am –10.30 am at daylight. Its result is that you are loved by the Gods, [and] all your activities are successful.
In the month of Veśākha (April-May), one takes a bath at around 10.30 am –12.00 pm. Its result is that the sorrow of the heart vanishes.
In the month of Jyeṣṭa (May-June), one takes a bath at around 10.30 am –12.00 pm. Its result is that all your activities are successful.
In the month of Aṣādha (June-July), one takes a bath at around 03.00 pm — 04.30 pm. Its result is having a lot of gold and silver. Such is the manner [of performing the observances].

This is called the ‘Pure Body’ (śarīra śuddha) and ‘Clean World’ (bhūmi śoca).This passage has two titles. The first, Adyus Anuṅku Rāt, meaning ‘Taking a Bath of Filling the World Completely’, appears at the beginning of the text. The second, ‘Pure Body’, ‘Clean World’ (Śarīra Śuddha, Bhūmi Śoca), appears at the end. I suspect that the first title refers to the process of performing the observance throughout the year, while the second title refers to the result of performing the observances.
There is the practice of ‘Following the Moon's Wisdom’ (Anīti Vulan):
1. In the first month (July-August), one does not eat any kind of tubers. Its result is that all plantings are successful.
In the second month (August-September), one does not eat beef. Its result is being rich in ox, [and] not being affected by disease.
In the third month (September-October), one does not eat pork. Its result is being rich in trees, not being affected by serious illness, [or] troubles.
In the fourth month (October-November), one does not eat any leaves. Its result is that all kinds of creepers and all kinds of hanging fruits will flourish.
In the fifth month (November-December), one does not quarrel, [and] does not carry a small child. Its result is that all your instructions given in a speech will be obeyed.
In the sixth month (December-January), one does not travel, [or does not take the same route] on the way back. Its result is being rich [and] having many servants (a whole bunch of servants).
In the seventh month (January-February), one does not eat cooked rice. Its result is being rich in paddy, not lacking the hoe.
In the eighth month (February-March), one does not eat meat of quadrupeds. Its result is being rich [and] all property will be increased.
In the ninth month (March-April), one does not eat dog [meat]. Its result is being handsome without make-up.
In the tenth month (April-May), one does not look up at the sky. Its result is that you will be smart.
In the Jyeṣṭa (May-June), one does not eat salt. Its result is being rich in land, not losing it even if it is asked for [by someone], [and] being obeyed and trusted [by people].

In the Saddhā (June-July), a man does not sleep with a woman, [and] a woman does not sleep with a man. Its result is being happy to have a husband, being loved by a man, and a man is loved by a woman, and all your speech will be obeyed [by people].
This is ‘The Holy Scripture for Being Accomplished’ (Aji Tutug) that should be known.
In the full moon of the first month (July-August), the Reverend Amūrva Bhuvana serves as [my] father. He is affectionate towards me.
In the full moon of the second month (August-September), the Reverend Madhu Sudhana serves as mother. He is affectionate towards me.

3. In the full moon of the third month (August-September), the Reverend Madhu Kusuma serves as my perfectly beautiful body, [and] is privileged to be obeyed by the supreme man; [who is] intelligent, wise; happy and rich.

In the full moon of the fourth month (September-October), the Reverend Asmara serves as my man: a handsome and wise warrior; supreme man; smart, happy, rich, [and who] overcomes the enemy. He is affectionate towards me.
In the full moon of the fifth month (October-November), the Reverend Manobhava serves as my eldes sont, [and] a handsome warrior. He is affectionate towards me.
In the full moon of the sixth month (November-December), the Reverend Atanu serves as my second brother, who is happy and rich. He is affectionate towards me.
In the full moon of the seventh month (December-January), the Reverend Kāmajaya serves as my third brother. He is affectionate towards me.
In the full moon of the eighth month (January-February), the Reverend Kāma Ratih serves as my youngest brother, who is happy [and] rich. He is affectionate towards me.
In the full moon of the ninth month (February-March), the Reverend Kumara serves as my relative when I was the bride and bridegroom, [and] became a wife and husband.
In the full moon of the tenth month (March-April), the Reverend Amadhapa serves as my fellow during my pregnancy.

In the full moon of the Jyeṣṭa (April-May), the Reverend Kumara serves as my first son who is a handsome warrior; he is my beloved; a supreme man, smart and wise, winning over enemy. He pays attention to me.
In the full moon of the Aṣādha (June-July), the Reverend Komari as my second daughter who is perfectly beautiful, happy [and] being obeyed by a supreme man, smart and wise. he pays attention to me.

My result [of performing] the ‘The Holy Scripture for Being Accomplished’ (Aji Tutug) is obtaining knowledge to complete [the role of] a father, mother; to be complete as a husband and wife; to be complete as a children and relatives, to be complete as a grand father and grand mother, to be complete as grand child and great-grandfather.
This continues into the future, making me handsome [and] beautiful, perfect, privileged and obeyed, happy and rich in paddy and wealthy in gold, jewels, dodot (garment worn around the lower part of the body), lәmәs ( soft clothing material).
I have many servants, livestock including four-legged and two-legged animals. I am rich and not affected by envy. I am successful in all my aims, [and] all my journeys. I will obtain goodness in the future reincarnations, and presently. The Bhagavan Panyarikan should have written it down. The Reverend Triyodaśa Sakṣi will be a witness. The Lord Hyaṅ Kabayan will be witnessing.

This is the right way to perform the observance in the fourth month (October-November), on the first day of the bright lunar fortnight (especially during the waning moon). The offering [presented] at each shrine is one dandanan śuci Dandanan: a set of offerings containing peras panyeneng combined with bebangkit (KBI, 2016: 218). Suci: offerings used in small ceremonies, consisting of white and yellow cakes (KBI, 2016: 939). The pupula Pupula is a specific type of ritual foliage or woven greenery utilized in ancient traditional Balinese offerings (sesayut). Positioned at the base of the altar during worship, it symbolizes natural fertility and spiritual blessing, which is later transferred to sanctify personal spaces like the sleeping quarters (https://e-museum.klungkungkab.go.id/id/). [and] colourful flowers are placed below. They should be placed in front of the person who performs the ritual worship. After finishing the worship, [the practitioner] should be sprinkled with holy water, then fast for full day and night. The pupulaSee the note above. and colourful flowers afterwards carried to the sleeping place to decorate it. Later, at 07.30—09.00 until 15.00—16.30, one should eat yellow cooked rice, [accompanied] by fried duck meat cooked with saurSaur: a side dish made from grated coconut that has been fried or dry-roasted, mixed with spices and a little sugar (KBI, 2016: 865).. If duck [meat] is unavailable, it [can be replaced with] [a duck] egg, [and] salt. During a fourteen-day interval, one does not touch any impurity. This state is called ‘without couple’ (asidhampati). (asidhampati).

Now, during the full moon of the fourth month (October-November), if one wishes to worship Smara, the place to perform the observance is an adorn pavilion in the waiting area. If the [practitioner] is young, they wear yellow clothes. If [the practitioner] is elder, they wear white clothes, clear [clothes], together with a set or suit of clothing. After purifying oneself through bathing, offerings should be presented at the shrine: two complete daṇḍananSee the note above. together with caturCatur: an offering consisting of cakes, bananas, sugar cane, tapai, rice, fish, side dishes and cloth, each in one of four colours (red, white, yellow, black), intended for the four deities (KBI, 2016: 172).; limas aguṅLimas aguṅ: an offering vessel made from coconut fronds, shaped like a pyramid, used to hold large quantities of nuts. is added with yellow cooked rice and the meat of a fried duck that is shaped as if it were still alive. It is called gegembon. Eggs with the shells removed is weared by kampuh cicirupanKampuh cicirupan: red garment worn around the lower part of the body (see also wastra) (OJED, s.v.)., and stuck with the tәlәṅ flower (Clitoria ternatea). These should be layered on the limas aguṅSee the note above.. The teteboganTetebogan: a hat-shaped container for yellow rice, woven from palm fronds (KBI, 2016: 988) should be added by yellow cooked rice, with sasahurSee the note above , and meat of a fried duck that is shaped as if it were still alive. It should be placed on daluvaṅ Daluvaṅ: clothing of bark cloth (worn by hermits etc) (OJED, s.v.)., written by the vowel (svara) and consonant (vyañjana) scripts. Each offerings presented at the Ibu Dәṅәn shrine should be completed by daṇḍananSee the note above. Offerings to the well are one rice cone, lalampadanLampad: an offering on the sacred banten consisting of nuts and side dishes (KBI, 2016: 542), sasamuhanSamuh: a cake made from rice flour and shaped by hand, used as an offering (KBI, 2016: 646).,holy water (taḍah pavitra). The offerings placed below represent the contents of the sea, including the pupulaSee the note above. and colourful flowers.

Once all the offerings have been placed, it should be washed with flowers. Then, the Daṅ Guru will begin worshipping in honour of the Sun God. As always, the practitioner will worship to the Sun, Moon, Shrine, Ibu Dәṅәn, until the well. The worship is performed in the evening, mid night, and in the early morning. After finishing the worship, the practitioner of the observance should be asked to take a bath to purify their body. And then, the practitioner is purified accompanied by pәras, sprinkled with holy water, [and reciting the mantra] to be victorious. [The ritual] is finished.

At the end the observance, the offerings are as follows: padamәlPadamel: an offering consisting of items that convey different flavours, such as bitter, sweet, salty, sour, spicy and savoury (KBI, 2016: 216)., sәga livәtSәga Livәt: rice cooked in a pot, not steamed; also: cooked thus (of other food)? (OJED, s.v.). The technique to make livәt rice is: the steamer should be marked with a lotus motif. After it has been prepared, the eggs should be poured in a baggage, [and then,] covered. Once it is cooked, it should be placed in the tapi (a round tray), and cast with spells of victory. [After that,] it is mixed with various vegetables—it is better if the practitioner can obtain the 108 colours.The earthen vessel (paruko) should also be decorated with a lotus motif. The cooked rice linivәt should be layered with vegetables and rice cone. It should be added by a whole aromatic nutmeg (jәbug arum). When adding hot water to the half-cooked rice (before steaming it for the second time), it should be sprinkled with honey and milk.The meat is the skin of the water buffalo yos baraṇaYos Bәrana/Yos Mәrana: a buffalo with black skin and white hair, or vice versa (KBI, 2016: 446).. It should be covered with leaves and nutmeg (jәbug arum). All of them should be cut into pieces entirely. And then, do not sleep during the day. Such is its excellence [of the observance], [that it should be] performed completely.

Thus, its result is that all kinds of disease, evil, and danger will vanish. All enjoyment will be found, mankind will be attracted, as it will be perfectly beautiful. Heaven will be found, as will final liberation. It should be accompanied by good deeds: not violating any prohibitions, obedience to parents, kind words, not speaking harshly; being constantly awake, performing the observance at the right time, and steadfastness in the right knowledge.
The food called dish of honey (madhu-parka), is provided with the presence of all the gods; knowing it as an offering, it is provided with the presence of all the gods.
The meaning is: the gods are present in the reverend dish of honey (madhuparka); you should only pay attention to them and feel [their presence].
God Viṣṇu is in the honey, Brahmā is reputed to be in the butter, and it is said that Īśvara is in the milk; and Mahā­deva is [in] the banana.
The meaning is: Viṣṇu is the deity associated with honey, Brahmā is the deity associated with sugar cane juice, Īśvara is the deity associated with milk, Mahādeva is the deity associated with banana.

In the salt of the sea, Rudra is immanent, Rice wine is associated with Guru, Śambhu, the say, is immanent in writing, In pinchbeck (?) you must know, Śiva is immanent, These are the substances in which the gods are immanent.

The meaning is: The deity of salt is Rudra, the deity of rice wine is Guru, the deity of water leaves is Śambhu and the deity of river water is Śiva. These are the deities present in the honey dish (madhuparka).
The butter burns the father’s evil, and the honey the mother’s evil; the milk burns one’s own excessive evil, and the banana, the evil done by one's relatives.

The meaning is: The sins of the father will vanish because of the sugar cane water. These are destroyed by them. The sins of the mother will vanish because of honey. These are destroyed by them. The sins of your body will vanish because of milk. The sins of your brother/sister, relatives, and wider group will vanish because of the banana.
This is why one should pay attention to the honey mantra (madhuparka). The mantra is: “This is auspicious dish of honey, a purifier which destroys evil, is created bt Īśvara; it purifies the whole world. Mam̐ three times! One should eat three times, and cleanse oneself!”
This is auspicious dish of honey, a purifier which destroys evil, is created bt Īśvara; it purifies the whole world. Mam̐ three times! One should eat three times, and cleanse oneself.
[However,] before doing this, one should first tend the God in the prescribed manner, and then fasts. After performing ritual worship for God, one should worship Him as laid down in observance.

“Hail to the Goddess Ṅhadvakadvaka!” In the east, “Om̐ hail to the goddess Mamakī, who battles with flowers!” In the south, “Om̐ hail and offerings to the goddess who possesses the ten powers (kadārpa daśapadha), svāhā!” In the west, “Om̐ obeisance to the goddess who blinds the mind of women!” In the middle, “Om̐ hail to the goddess Makaradhvajamandorathā, svāhā!” In the north, Om̐ hail to the goddess who shatters the essence of the mantra!”
This is the ‘Reverend of Eight Goddess.’
“Om̐ hail to the God of Gods, Smara! Om̐ hail to Indra! Om̐ Om̐ hail to Svaṣti!”
“Thou art visible here in this world. Thou art human and also a god; Thou art subtle and also divisible. Thou art inner self and outer body!”
“Thou art unique in form and without particularities. Thou possessest an easy seat within the goddess of the heart; always unique like the Moon, Thou art able to conquer the threefold cosmos!”
“Thou prevailest over God ĩśvara, Thou also conquerest Brahmā definitely; Thou prevailest also over Mahā-deva, Thou also obtainest a complete victory over Viṣṇu!”
“And Thou art the wishing-Stone of Indra, Thou art the King of all young men; Thus Thou art is called King Kumāra. Thou art served by all the goddesses!”
“Thou shalt remove all evils for perfection, O God, King Kumāra; Thou removest all diseases, and destroyest all enemies!”
Hymne to the God of Love.

This is the right behaviour to perform [the observance] of the night of Śiva. First, you should begin with an ordinary daytime Sun Salutation (sūrya sevana). When you have completed the Sun Salutation (sūrya sevana), go to the place of worship (pamiyosan), and sit down reverently in front of the pedestal of the god (pīṭā). If there is no such pedestal, substitute it with the tip of banana leaves. If there is a golden liṅga, (or) yellow silver, worship the god and bring Him down into the tip of banana leaves, especially in the pedestal of the god. It should be worshipped there.
One should be performed the padmāsana and other, including the deva pratiṣṭha. The lord should be invoked from the heart. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Mam̐ Am̐ Um̐!” Envisage the reverend one descending into the liṅga. Carry out the rite, using grains of rice, sandal wood, and young maja or flowers.
The lord should be then firmly installed (reinstalled) again in the liṅga. If there is no gold, [it can be changed by] silver. If there is no silver, [it can be changed by] the quintessence of white vaduri. Make it into a liṅga. The installation mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Am̐ Um̐ Mam̐!”
The young maja leaves, all kinds of flowers, sandalwood, and grains of rice should be worshipped. Fortunate if the incense, light, and ganta are worshipped. The ganitri should be recited [with the mantras], together with breath control (prāṇāyama), and devotion (sәmbah). Your mantra This text seems to make the word liṅ and mantra as a synonym is: “Om̐ Om̐ hail to Liṅga-Liṅgādipati!”
You should also offer aromatics, flowers, incense, the light, divers fruits, and sәḍah voh. Your words while offering them are: “Om̐ Om̐ Śiva! I offer naivedya and caru offerings. Accept their essence as amṛta. Sa Ba Ta A I. Hail to Śiva. A U Ma, Om̐. [The rite] should be worshipped three times. The first is in the evening, [the second is] at midnight, [the third] is in the early morning. While carrying out the rite, you must continually recite the mantras: “Om̐ Om̐ hail to Liṅga, Om̐ hail to the Sadāśivaliṅga!” In the early morning (before sunrise), He should be returned to the lotus of your innermost part, using the mantra: “Oṁ hail to the Atma Liṅga, Om̐ Om̐ hail to the Am̐ Mam̐!”

This is the final mantra [for performing the observance]: “Om̐! Hail to Śiva, the Śiva-liṅga; to Śiva, the great Lord of all; hail to the divine Śiva; O Sadāśiva, hail to you; Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśvara are the divine; the omniscient Supreme Lord (Parameśvara) is the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution; to the Liṅga-deva, hail, hail!”
The mantra is applicable for all kinds of finishing procedures.
If you wish to briefly [perform the observance] of the Night of Śiva, your mantras [to beginning] is:

“Om̐ Om̐ hail to the Lord of Liṅgas. Om̐ Om̐ hail to the Ātma-liṅga!” The evening worship is: “Om̐ Om̐ hail to the Paramaśiva-Liṅga!” The midnight worship is: “Om̐ Om̐ hail to the Śūnya Liṅga!” The early morning worship [should be performed] by honouring the sprout of maja, the praise is at the same time: “Om̐ hail to Śiva! hail to Rudra, [hail] to the motionless mountain!”

Do not be affected by the tamah [any] kind of observance performed. Tamah means ‘sleep.’ It should be overpowered, [and] do not forget this when you are performing the observance. Also, you do not sleep during the day. It is forbidden! All your results in performing the observance will vanish, all the observances will be unfruitful, [and] all the intentions will not be reached. That is why, attention should be paid to it. Do not regard it as unimportant [because] religious austerity and observance will produce great results. Worldly happiness will be found because of it. The state of yogīśvara, [and] final liberation as its result. Therefore, do not criticise those who perform the observance [and] religious austerity. Do not insult [memeṅeniṅ] those who perform the observance. It is forbidden, as said by the holy scripture.

This is the observance of ‘Sacred Teachings on the Quintessence of Galuṅan’ (Aji Sāriniṅ Galuṅan). The right behaviour to [perform this observance is to present] offerings at the shrine. The complete bantәn śuci at the Ibu Dәṅәn. All of these are given one by one. For the water is one piece. The water is given as one piece. Recite the introduction mantra, then perform the worship using kavaṅi (flowers). The mantra is: “Om̐, may I become victorious and famous, be rich without working, and akaravaṅan, its appearance is red, its size is a small flit (arәṅit).” That is the quintessence of the Galuṅan, which serves as my relative. All of people who knows the quintessence of Galuṅan is my followers, all around the world, [and] in the whole area of the world. All of people who knows the quintessence of Galuṅan is my brother (sister), [and] as my friend. All my provision (money) to know the quintessence of Galuṅan is twenty five thousands, two hundred and fifty thousand, twenty five yuta, as my provision (money). It will be found now. It will be found presently. The goodness will be found presently. It will come in one thousand and one day. “Om̐ Sa Ba Ta A I, hail to Śiva, A U Ma Om̐!”

This is the observance of ‘The Quintessence of Galuṅan’ (Añarin Galuṅan). Its right way is to present a jrimpәn Jrimpәn: an offering made from an upright cylindrical basket, filled with sweets, fruit and a small basket containing rice, betel leaves, white thread and money; on top of the basket is placed a special sampian Sampian: a garland of palm fronds forming part of the offering (KBI, 2016: 844) for the jrimpen (KBI, 2016: 411) offering at each [shrine] on the Galuṅan day. It should be placed in front of the shrine. The offerings [to be present] at the shrine are the same as before. For the Ibu shrine in the middle, For the Ibu shrine in the middle, fragrant cosmetic unguent (burat vaṅi), sesame oil (lәṅa vaṅi), two portions of rice, and 225 coins should be added. All of these [offerings] should be honoured and worshipped. After finishing the worship, one eats the jrimpәnSee the note above.. After eating the jrimpәnSee the note above., one can eat according to one's ability. The honouring (pūjā/mantra) when eating jrimpәnSee the note above. is: “Om̐ the Goddess of Sarīniṅ Galuṅan, your man who has already known the quintessence of Galuṅan will absorb the quintessence of the day, absorb the quintessence of the night, absorb the quintessence of the illustrious Sādhana, absorb all kinds of pollen (flowers), [and] absorb the quintessence of all the world. I know the quintessence of the Galuṅan, I can be a superior bhujaṅgaBhujaṅga: a brahman or other person of clerical rank. In older texts it often appears to be a younger brahman (student or disciple); later (Maja-Pahit and after) a religious official (śaiva or boddha, but distinct from vipra and ṛṣi)., [and] be a relative of the king. I can be a happy and rich person, until my children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren will obey me. This will continue to my children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, until all my sect. The Reverend Triyodaśa Sakṣi will be my witness.” Its result is that all your activities will be reach goodness, be loved by Bhūta Dәṅәn, and all your family will feel comfortable in the house.

There is the observance of ‘Having Amusement’ (Asusukhan): on the full moon of the seventh month, seven times a day, [and] seven times in one night; one eats, drinks, [and] dances. The Lord of Kapitu gives the observance. Its result is that one is happy, rich with children [and] companions, has a long life, [as well as] being obeyed and trusted [by the people].
There is the observance of being fed according to the month. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is being loved by the people.
There is the observance of eating across the month by compressing [the food] with the whole hand. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that one is famous, [and] loved by women.

There is the observance of ‘Many Moons’The alternative for this translation is ‘Fresh Moon’ because the word mahu can be defined as ‘just, only recently, freshly’ (OJED, s.v) (Mahucandra): One applies kohl every Monday, especially on Wednesday Irәṅ Also known in Balinese as Buddha Cәmәṅ (Black Wednesday)., and Sunday Manis, especially it should [be applied by one] continuously. The deity is Reverend Maṇik Bade. Its appointed duration is three years and three months. Its result is that the Reverend Candra [and] Aditya love [you]. [You will not be] vague, seen in good condition, and most lustrousThis result probably refers to the charismatic effect after one performs the observance..

There is the observance of ‘Following the Star’ (Ṅlintaṅ): one does not eat if the star with seven relatives (lintaṅ pipitu sānak)This constellation refers to Pleiades (or the Big Dipper), also renowned as Bintaṅ Kārttika (October-November). has not appeared yet. Its appointed duration is half a month. Its result is that one will be rich in the future, and your appearance will not be lusterless.

There is the observance of one eats only in the evening right after the time of approaching twilight. It is called the observance of ‘Without Having the Torch’ (Tan Pasuluh). It serves as the appearance, [and] as the speech of all people. Its result is that all your aims will be reached.

There is the observance of not eating at the time around 09.00 — 10.30 am in the morning, not chewing the betel [and] not drinking water. After ending the time at 09.00 — 10.30 am, one is able to chew betel, eat, and drink. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is that one is rich in the landThe word bhuvana means 'world' (OJED, s.v.), but I have translated it as 'land' to make it appropriate for this context., and the appearance is handsome.

There is the observance of eating every time around 09.00 — 10.30 am in the morning. [At this time,] one is able to eat, drink, and chew betel. Its result is that one is happy [and] rich when at a young age, [and] accomplished in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of ‘Being Good’ (Ṅayu): one does not eat when the sun is already in the west and [all light of] Reverend Sun has already set. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity of this observance is the Reverend Prabhaṅkāra. Its result is that you [will] enjoy your youth, [and] all your aims will be accomplished.
There is the observance of eating in the sleeping place when the sun is shining brightly. Its result is that one will be happy to have a husband.

There is the observance of eating flowers every Umanis: all kinds of flowers are collected with salt and charcoal, [and] the tip of betel leaf. When eating it in the sleeping place, one faces the head of the bed, [and] when eating it [the time is] at the 07.00—07.30 am in the morning. Its result is that one [will be] handsome with many people being dazed [at him]; if a woman performs [this observance], she will be happy to have a husband [and] be loved in the sleeping place. When eating, one faces to the head of bed.This passage contains a textual redundancy regarding the instructions for the observance, specifically repeating the requirement to face the head of the bed.

There is the observance of the ‘Intermediate Meal’ (Antarabhakta): one eats at the midday, [or] if in the evening when people are sleeping. Its appointed duration is five months. Its result is that one becomes tisan kuras, being greatly pleased by learned man.

There is the observance of ‘Gaining the Victory’ (Añjaya): one does not eat in the afternoon. Its appointed duration is one year and seven days. The deity is the Reverend Kr̥ta Bhuvana. Its result is that the world is prosperous, crop disease become harmless, one [will possess] supernatural power, be loved by God, [as well as] followed by all kinds of wildness.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like a Lotus Stalk’ (Anrus Tuñjuṅ): during the full moon of the seventh month (January-February), one takes a bath seven times a day, [and] seven times a night. When the waning moon is on the 14th, one performs a ritual on the night of Śiva by presenting an offering in the form of one set of śuci. The deity is Lord Guru. Its result is that all your obstacles [will] disappear, and you [will] be loved by the Bhūta Dәṅәn, loved by your master, and by all people.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like a Lotus Stalk’ (Anrus Tuñjuṅ): one sleeps [and] stands up in one night. Lord Śiva gives the observance. Its result is possessing supernatural power. [If something] goes wrong, one [will be] reborn as a king, who is rich [and whose wealth will] not diminish even if it is requested [by the people]; having a fixed place in the region, there will be no people who are succeeed in attacking him.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like a Lotus Stalk’ (Anrus Tuñjuṅ): when it is the fifth day of the waxing moon in the seventh month (January-February), one extinguishes the fire, and then abstains from eating food and sleeping for one day and one night. The deity of the observance is Lord Aśih Prāṇa. Its result is that one [will] possess supernatural power, [and] harvest all the quintessence of the observance.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like a Lotus Stalk’ (Anrus Tuñjuṅ): one takes a bath three times a night, seven times a day, [and] sleeps in a leaning [position]. Its result is that one [will] know all the qualities of all people; be handsome without equal, and become the head of warriors all around the world.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like a Lotus Stalk’ (Anrus Tuñjuṅ): one takes a bath three times a night, [and] three times a day, without sleeping in a lying-down position, [but only] in a leaning position. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is that one [will] always know the qualities of all people; be a warrior who is handsome without equal; [and] become the master of weapons; without equal among all people in the world, all the other islands in Nūsāntara [will] look up to him.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like a Lotus Stalk’ (Anrus Tuñjuṅ): one takes a bath seven times a day, [and] seven times a night. Its result is that one [will be] perfectly beautiful, received by the king, [and] loved by learned men.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like a Lotus Stalk’ (Anrus Tuñjuṅ): one takes a bath, seven times a day and [seven times] at night. You [should] chew betel leaves every large moonThe phrase vulan aguṅ in this context probably refers to the brilliant light of the full moon. The other possibility is that it denotes a stage of the year when the months have reached higher numbers, such as the ninth, tenth, eleventh, or twelfth month.. Its result is that you [will be] knowledgeable, [and] all your behavior [will be free] from hesitation, [and all people] in the world [will be] in tumultuous confusion over you.

There is the observance of ‘The Three Junctions’ (Trisandhyā): one eats three handfuls [of food] a day. Its appointed duration is three years. Its result is reaching the heaven of Lord Viṣṇu. [If something] goes wrong, one [will be] reborn as a perfectly beautiful person, [and enjoy] great happiness.

There is the observance of ‘The Three Junctions’ (Trisandhyā): one takes a bath three times a day, and [three times] at night. After taking a bath, one should chew a quid (hold a susur between the teeth), [and apply] kohl. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is reaching Indra's heaven. [If something] goes wrong, one [will be] reborn as a perfectly beautiful [and] wise person.

There is the observance of ‘Taking a Bath Like the Point of a Lance’ (Kakaracan Adyus): one takes a bath all day and all night. Its kohl is oil. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Indra; [and] being reborn as a perfectly wise person, and a completely handsome youth.

There is the observance of eating all kinds of raw [food]. The deity of the observance is Bhagavān Aṅgasti. Its result is that one becomes a God. [If something] goes wrong, one [will] become a king who is loved by God; [and] a warrior who defeats all enemies, with no one being his equal. One is never separated from performing this observance.

There is the observance of ‘Conducting Purification’ (Aśuci Lakṣaṇa): one does not eat before washing one’s face, [and] applying oil. Its result is that one [will be] handsome and attract others when conducting the observance; one’s hair becomes soft, [and] one’s speech and appearance become pleasant.

There is the observance of ‘Conducting Purification’ (Nuci Lakṣaṇa): one adorns oneself first before eating. Its result is that you [will be] an object of attraction in all your conduct, [your body will be] thin [and] adroit; as well as being happy with your husband.

There is the observance of wearing śuddha mala clothes. The mantra is: “Om̐, O purified of sin, O purified of impurity!” [Repeat] three [times]. “O purified, O purified, O one whose purity is restored! O purified, O purified, O essence of restored purity!” Its result is that your impurity and misfortune, sin and pain will vanish. Its appointed duration of this observance is thirteen days. One receives [this observance] during the dark moon. The means [of offering] is: flower of śuddha mala leaves, [and] the leaves should be counted. Its mantra is sufficiently treated as the calculation [of the leaves].

There is the observance when on the first day of the waxing moon, second day of the waxing moon, [and] third day of the waxing moon, one wears a śuddhamala sarong, [and] saci’s clothes after finishing [eating] the labahanLabahan is: a kind of offering for spirits (KBI, 2016: 532). Its result is that your appearance [will be] slender, [and] perfectly handsome. If a man performs this observance, he will be courted for marriage by a woman. If a woman [performs it], she will be courted for marriage by a man. The name of this observance is ‘The Appearance of a Bull’ (Andakarūpa).

There is the observance of ‘Eating Fruits’ (Malāhara): if one eats the mangosteen, durian, [and] all kinds of fruit. Its appointed duration is three months. Its result is reaching the heaven of Lord Guru, and the Lord Saḍāśiva. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a rich [and] virtuous person.

There is the observance of chewing the rhizom of tәmu ros beteltәmu: a rhizomatous plant with leaves resembling those of turmeric (Curcuma longa), utilized in traditional herbal medicine (jamu), porridge, and various other preparations. Variants include: -- gongséng, a temu variety characterized by small, bell-shaped (giring-giring) rhizome nodules; -- ireng (Curcuma aeruginosa), a variety distinguished by its dark/blackish interior; -- kedis, a variety bearing small, yellowish rhizomes; -- konci (Boesenbergia rotunda), a smaller, low-growing variety with yellowish rhizomes; -- lawak (Curcuma zanthorrhiza), widely used as the primary ingredient for the temulawak beverage; and -- tis (Curcuma purpurascens), a variety whose rhizomes closely resemble turmeric., the pinang nut cannot be touched touched by the knife (ladiṅ), [and] is hit by the betel-leaf, with the powdered lime. Its result is that one is firm without having a guardian, and is obeyed [by the people].

There is the observance of not eating the pinang nut that is not cutted off a half by the ladiṅ. Its result is that one is not penetrated by all kinds of the sharp [weapon], being victorious in the battle without being difficult.
There is the observance of [using] stone on which food is served when performing the observance. Its result is that one is firm in arm, skin, and strength.
There is the observance of eating a handful [of food]. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that you will be loved by mankind.
There is the observance of eating two handfuls [of food]. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that one will not be difficult [in reaching] the quality.
There is the observance of eating three handfuls [of food]. Its appointed duration is three nights. Its result is being loved by mankind, always increasing without decreasing.
