There is the observance of ‘Threefold Commitment’ (Trisamaya): one eats three handfuls of cooked rice. Its appointed duration is one month. The Reverend Tiga gives the observance. Its result is that one will be loved by the learned man, [and] the quality of mantra is powerful.

There is the observance of ‘Threefold Commitment’ (Trisamaya): one eats three handfuls [of food] in one day. Its appointed duration is three years. Its result is reaching the abode of the Lord Viṣṇu. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a perfectly beautiful person, [and] great happiness.
There is the observance of ‘Single Meal’ (Ekabhakta): one eats a handful of meals. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that the effort will be obtained quickly.
There is the observance of eating seven handfuls [of food]. Its appointed duration is seven days. The Lord Gaṇa gives the observance. Its result is being loved by all mankind.
There is the observance of eating twelve handfuls [of food]. Its result is that your activity [will be] successful. The name of such observance is ‘being enjoy’ (Amukti).

There is the observance of eating the kupat kәpәt with every kind of śuci as the meat. Its appointed duration is three nights. It is called ‘intoxication of plucky’ (aṅlakimada). The Reverend Īśvara descends to perform the observance. He becomes the appearance, the voice of singing, the sweetness of speech, [and] a female brahmin gives the palm leaf manuscript. Its result is having received a gift or favour in the world, [and] many [people] love you.

There is the observance of eating kupat kәpәl. Its meat is only one, namely every kind of śuci. Its appointed duration is three nights. It is called ‘being river site’ (aṅalipada). The Reverend Īśvara descends to perform the observance. Its result is that he serves as appearance, serves as the sound of a song, and [serves as] the sweetness of talking.

There is the observance of eating kupat kәpәl seven seeds. One eats in daylight: two [balls] is in the morning , three [balls] is in the evening, [and] two [balls] is in the noon. Its meat is the content of the river. Its appointed duration is one month. Its result is that one is guarded by the king, being loved by the people, [and feeling] the happiness presently.

There is the observance of eating a handful [of food] when the amount of meal is one pinch [of food] between the fingertips. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is being loved by mankind, and being disposed kindly by the people. The name of such observance is ‘Single’ (Ekāki).

There is the observance of sleeping in the stand upright [position], it is better if one can stand on one foot at the same time. If you eat a handful [of food] in one day, [and] if you drink a little water, its appointed duration is three nights. Its result is that one [has competency] in speaking together with the God, evidently powerful [and] reaching the final liberation.

There is the observance of eating two handfuls [of food]. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that one’s quality will be reached suddenly without facing difficulty. The name of such observance is ‘sleeping’ (anidrā).

There is the observance of eating three handfuls [of food]. Its appointed duration is three months and three nights. Its result is being loved by mankind. The name of such observance is ‘Threefold Commitment’ (Trisamaya).

There is the observance of ‘Being the Five Joys’ (Amañcagәmә): one eats five handfuls of cooked rice continuously. Its appointed duration is five months. Its result is being loved by all people, having attained the eight qualities; having valour; being renowned, rich, and having a powerful mantra.

There is the observance of eating seven handfuls [of food]. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that your quality will be reached suddenly; you are not affected by all kinds of poisons. The name of such observance is ‘Four Faces’ (Caturmukha)
There is the observance of eating seven handfuls [of food]. Its appointed duration is four months. Its result is that one will taste happiness in the future.

There is the observance of eating nine handfuls [of food] every full moon. It is called ‘Livelihood Maintenance’ (Mr̥tiāhāṛa). It should be obtained in the ninth month (kasaṅa) for three successive [months]. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Indra. [If something] goes wrong one is reborn as the perfectly beautiful person, [and] being rich from childhood.

There is the observance of eating sixteen handfuls [of food]. It should be eaten once! Its appointed duration is sixteen months. Its result is that you will not be affected by any kind of pain or illness. The name of such observance is ‘Being Long’ (Adavā).

There is the observance of ‘every seventh month’ (aṅapitu): one eats seven handfuls [of food]. It should be eaten in the seventh month for three successive [months]. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Brahmā. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a rich person from childhood, [and] perfectly beautiful.

There is the observance of every Sunday Umanis. One eats a handful of rice cooked for three successive Sunday Umanis. Its result is that one will be easy to have children, go right through until the child, grand child, [and] great-grandchild; they will be happy, rich, and will not be deceived [by something].

There is the observance of ‘Eating Rice with Water’(Añәkul Bañu): the manner is that one eats the cooked rice a handful in one day, two handfuls in tomorrow, three handfuls in the next two days. In the next three days one ends [the observance]. The mantra when eating is: “Om̐ free from desease, free from sin, free from impurity of my father and mother! [all of them] untied [and] eternally come back to the truth.” One eats without salt, [and] without meat. It is only affected by the water, without being touched by the lisah, without being touched by the powder, without chewing betel, without drinking palmwine, without sleeping in the noon, [and] without dispersing. Its result is that all kinds of pain and illness will vanish.

Again the observance of eating rice with water. One eats a handful [of food] in the palm's hollow, and the amount of water is in harmony with the size of the palm’s hollow. Its appointed duration is three days. It will be better in five days. Mantra: “kәbas is going back to the original condition.” Its result is free from pain and obstacles.

There is the observance of eating rice with water. To use as a means: the container in black colour as the base. The mantra is: Om̐, there is the hole without circle. There is the hole which is free from impurity, free from obstacles, [and] free from tears. Om̐ hail to lustrous Śri! Om̐ hail to Mam̐!” One should ask permission of the one who is in charge of the observance in the shrine. The mantra is: “Om Mam̐ hail to Īśvara!”

There is the observance of ‘Eating Rice with Water’ (Añәkul Bañu): one eats on the palm's hollow. Its appointed duration is seven nights. [The food] is cooked rice and water. The mantra is: Om̐, free from illness, free from sin, free from father [and] mother! Unfasten and departed [from all of them], going back to its reality! Unfasten all kinds of bodily sin, as well as the sins of father and mother!

There is the observance of eating rice with water, [and] entering it five [times]. The rice cooked should be shaped into one ball, [and] the water should be drunk in one go. The rice cooked should be shaped into one ball again, [and] the water should be drunk in one go. Its limit is three times (It should be repeated three times). Afterwards, one can eat whatever one desires. After eating, one drinks the water, and then rinses and wash one's hands, as well as chew the betel leaf with it on the one's belly. Thus is the manner [of this observance]. [The duration is] according to one's willingness. Its excellent duration is one year. The mantra os: “Om̐ there is the hole without impurity, there is the hole without circle; it is free from obstacle, free from the tears, free from illness, [and] free from misfortune. All kinds of impurity disappeared.” Its result is that all kinds of impurity will vanish from your body; you will be loved by the king, and the god will love you.

There is the observance of eating rice with water. The mantra is: “Saṅ Drәmba Moha you should eat in the market; Saṅ Kāla Viṣaya you should eat in the place for gambling; Saṅ Kāla Ṅaḍaṅ you should eat in the big street, [and] Saṅ Kāḷa Katuṅ you should eat in the place for slaughtering. After eating, you should go back to my body [and] bones. Accompany me in doing the goodness. Om̐ Let there be success!”

There is the observance of not drinking water when eating if one is choking (faltering), until you finish eating in one go. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that your goal will not be faltered, the desire will come quickly to you.
There is the observance of not drinking water. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is having supernatural powers. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Padma.

There is the observance of eating from a vessel made of leaves. It is supported [from below] by the left hand, without being added [the food] to it. Its result is being loved by mankind, [until] in the end one does not drink water. [Its duration] is according to one's pleasure in performing the observance. Its result is one will obtain supernatural power [and] one's goal.
There is the observance of eating without adding [anything] to it. Its appointed duration is seven years. Its result is reaching great enjoyment.

There is the observance of not allowing [anything] to be added [when eating]. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is intelligent offspring who succeed in their activities. The name of such observance is ‘To Lessen’ (Aniraṅ).

There is the observance of not adding [the food], not drinking water. If one has finished chewing betel leaves, drinking water is allowed. [Its appointed duration] to perform the observance is according to one’s pleasure. Its result is that [you will be] a warrior.

There is the observance that one should eat the leaf. It should be held up [by the hand] without [leaving any] leftovers, [and] adding [anything]. Its appointed duration is three nights. It is called the 'lotus match'.The Reverend Campuriṅ Rāt, he who descends to perform the observance; he becomes a neck, finger, [and] nail; and then [its result is that you will be loved] by mankind.
There is the observance of eating without adding [anything]. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that your activity is successful, [and] being loved by mankind.

There is the observance of eating the long stalk of a palm (or banana-leaf) held up on the left hand without [leaving any] leftovers, [and] adding [anything]. The Reverend Ekṣaṣana descends to perform the observance. Its result is being loved by mankind.

There is the observance of not allowing [the addition of food during the meal]. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is having intelligent offspring who succeed in their activities. The name of such observance is ‘to lessen’ (Aṅiraṅ).
There is the observance of when one eats without [leaving any] leftovers, [and] adding [anything]. Its result is that you will not have an enemy in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of ‘Being Silence’ (Mona): when one eats without speaking. Its appointed duration is three years. Its deity is the Lord Rudra. Mantra: Om̐ hail to Rudra! [I take] leave. Its result is being respected by the world, [and] all your aims will be fulfilled.

There is the observance of eating in silence without drinking water. After eating, one drinks water, [and] will be allowed to speak. Its result is that one will not be affected by the illness, will be superior in the world, [as well as] will be obeyed and trusted [by the people]. Its appointed duration is seven months.

There is the observance of being silent when eating the food: one does not speak when eating. Its appointed duration is three years. Its deity is the Lord Rudra. Its result is that one will be rewarded by the all gods, [and] one’s quality will come.

There is the observance of being silent when eating, being silent when vapouring (nap), being silent when muris, being silent when chewing, being silent when applying holy ashes, being silent when sweeping, [and] being silent when defecating.
Further the result of being silent.
Be silent while eating: its result is that you are wise and have a long life.
Be silent while nap: its result is that you will be loved by mankind, kings, [and] priests.
Be silent while applying holy ashes, its result is reaching the [the heaven] of the Goddess Rātri. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a powerful priest.
Be silent while sweeping: its result is being loved by the learned man, and the king as a god, [and] being a good [person] in your reincarnation.
Be silent while defecating: its result is that your desires will be fulfilled quickly, and you will have many disciples.
Be silent while chewing: its result is that your activities will be successful, you will be lightened in the final liberation.
Be silent while muris: its result is that your activity will be successful, your desires will be met quickly.

There is the observance of ‘Five Faces’ (Pañcamukha): one being silent every evening on Kalivon. [This observance] embraces all other observances. Its result is that one will obtain great happiness, be reborn as one who is wealthy in rice, [and] enjoy it from childhood, [as well as] being obeyed by all mankind.

There is the observance of ‘Being Turmeric’ (Ṅunir): if one eats the cooked rice coloured by turmeric. Its appointed duration is according to one’s pleasure in performing the observance. Its deity is the Lord Mahādeva. Its result is reaching the heaven of lord Mahādeva. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a ship captain who is rich in money and slaves, [as well as] one is successful with the one who is his honourable.
There is the observance of eating turmeric as a side dish. It is called ‘Shooting Gold with an Arrow’ (Amanah Kañcana). Its result is being rich in gold.

There is the observance of ‘Being Yellow’ (Aṅuniṅ): the yellow rice is eaten by one. If it is not like that, one only eats turmeric as side-dish. Its appointed duration is seven years. Its deity is the Goddess Ratih. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Mahādeva. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a powerful ship captain.
There is the observance of ‘Being yellow’ (Ṅuniṅ): one eats the turmeric first. Its appointed duration is one month. Mantra: “Om̐ hail to nir!”

There is the observance of ‘Behaving Like Bhīma’ (Ambhīma): if one eats with salt as one’s side dish. Its appointed duration is one year and three months. Its deity is the Lord Īśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ mam̐ hail to Īśvara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that all one's desires will be fulfilled quickly; being loved by learned men; and the gods and demons will love you.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Bhīma’ (Ambhīma): one fasts on the 12th day of the waxing moon in the seventh month (kapitu). Its result is an abundance of happiness, and having powerful mantras; winning over enemies, being obeyed and trusted by mankind, [and] collecting all the countries of all people.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Bhīma’ (Ambhīma): if one eats with salt as a dish. In Umanis, one eats egg whites, [and] white onions. In Paing, one eats red glutinous rice, [and] red onions. In Pvan, one eats yellow rice, with a yellow egg as a dish. In Vage, one eats the black glutinous rice, [and] bakula as a dish. In Kalivon, one eats rice of the five colours, with various other foods as a dish. Its result is being rich in gold, silver, and iron.

There is the observance of ‘Silent when Sleeping in a Leaning Position’ (Mona Turu Suamaṇḍah). Its appointed duration is three months. Its deity is the lord Viṣṇu. The mantra is: “Om̐ Um̐ Um̐ hail to Viṣṇu!” Its result is tha you will receive gifts, [and] all your speech will be effective.

There is the observance of ‘Sleeping in a Leaning Position’ (Turu Sumaṇḍah). Its appointed duration is one month. The Lord Sambhu gives the observance. Its result is being handsome, young, [and] having a splendorous family.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Kumbhakarṇa’ (Aṅumbhakarṇa): one sleeps in a sloping position for one year. Its appointed duration is two years. Its deity is Devāntara. The mantra is: Om̐ hail to Devantara! [I take] leave. Its result is that one has many offspring, [and] all the live-stock become tame and fertile.

There is the observance of ‘Being Powerful’ (Kumavaśa): one does not sleep day and night for seven nights. Its result is that you will become a brave man; [and] all your activities will be successful, without facing any difficulty.

There is the observance of ‘Being a Mother’ (Niṅibu): one eats all kinds of ‘mother’ [of food]. Its appointed duration is four months. Its result is reaching the heaven of Lord Rudra. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as the son [of noble family] !Saṅ Kumbhakarṇa sleeps without powerlessly, day and night and then, fasts. Its result is being obeyed all your deeds [by the people].
There is the observance of not eating [and] not sleeping. Its deity is the Reverend Saṅ Hyaṅ Tan Kaviśeṣa. Its result is targeting heaven.

There is the observance of ‘Good Sleep’ (Lәvih Turu): one does not have a strong attachment to food. The deity of this observance is the Lord Keśava. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Śiva; being reborn as a son of a noble family, being free from pain [and] obstacles; [and] being perfectly famous.

There is the observance of fasting for seven nights, and then without falling asleep day [and] night. The deity of this observance is the Lord Śiva. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Śiva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one will become a brave man, all your works will be successful, and then one will have a supernatural power.

There is the observance of ‘Being a Hero’ (Ambīra): if one only eats salt as meat. Its appointed duration is one year and three months. Its deity is the Lord Iśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Īśvara!” Its result is all your desires will be fulfilled quickly; you will be loved by mankind; and god and demon love you.

There is the observance of 'Being Raw Food' (Aṅlavar): one does not eating [the food] that has been salted. Its appointed duration is one year. Its deity is Lord Śaṅkara. Its result is reaching the heaven [of Indra]. [If something] goes wrong, you will be reborn as a beautiful [and] wise person.

There is the observance of ‘Being Raw Food’ (Ṅlavar): one does not eat salt. Its appointed duration is four months [and] four nights. Its result is reaching the heaven [of Indra]. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a perfectly beautiful person.

There is the observance of ‘Fasting’ (Aṅupavāsa): one eats by biting salt [and] charcoal first. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity of this observance is the Goddess Gaṅga. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Gaṅga!” Its result is that all your deeds will be obeyed by the world.

There is the observance of eating rice cones with salt [and] charcoal as meat. Its deity is the Lord Īśvara. He becomes appearance, [and] becomes the voice of a song and story. Its result is the sweetness of the mouth.

There is the observance of eating flowers every Umanis, with salt [and] charcoal as meat. After eating, one chews the tip of betel leaves. It is called the ‘Wearing the Sign of Flowers’ (Aṅliṅga Kәmbaṅ). Its result is that one will be happy and rich; as well as one will have an extraordinary appearance.
There is the observance of eating without salt. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that your supernatural power will come, and then you will be respected by God.

There is the observance of ‘Eating like Sarasvatī’ (Arasoti): one eats salt [and] charcoal as meat. Its appointed duration is seven days. The deity of this observance is the Goddess Sarasoti. Its result is wisdom.
This is the ‘Flourishing Month’ (Kr̥ta Māsa): it is a good time for me to perform the good [deeds], especially the group of observance in following the teaching.

In the first month (July-August) on the tenth day of the waxing month. Its deity is the Reverend Vīra Kusuma, its observance is that you do not eat any kinds of tubers. Its result is that you will become rich, youth, and rich in children.

In the second month (August-September) on the seventh day of the waxing month, its deity is the Reverend Jaya Kusuma. Its observance is that one does not eat beef. Its result is freedom from tuju, tәluh, [and] tarañjana; [as well as] becoming rich in live-stock.

In the third month (September-October) on the ninth day of the waxing month, its deity is the Reverend Naka. Its observance is that one does not eat pork. Its result is that one does not attacked by serious illness.

In the fourth month (October-November) on the fifteenth day of the waxing month, its deity is the Reverend Asmara. Its observance is that one does not eat any leaves. Its result is that all [of plants] planted by you will be successful.

In the fifth month (November-December), on the fifteenth day of the waning moon, its deity is the Reverend Mahādeva. Its observance is that one [should] not speak harshly, [and] carry a child in both arms. Its result is that one will have many children.

In the sixth month (December-January), on the eighth day of the waning moon, its deity is the Reverend Atanu. Its observance is that one should not spend the night while travelling. Its result is that one will become rich without losing [wealth].

In the seventh month (January-February), on the thirteenth day of the waxing moon, its deity is the Reverend Manasija. Its observance is that one eats food [especially edible roots and fruit]. Its result is becoming rich and being obeyed [by the people]; [as well as acquiring] all desirable qualities.

In the eighth month (February-March), on the second day of the waxing moon, its deity is the Reverend Anaṅgara. Its observance is that one does not eat the meat of quadrupeds. Its result is [becoming] rich in domestic animals.

In the ninth month (March-April), on the sixth day of the waxing moon, its deity is the Reverend Ravi. Its observance is that one does not eat dog meat. Its result is [becoming] a handsome [and] attractive warrior.

In the tenth month (April-May), on the fourth day of the waxing moon, its deity is the Reverend Brahmā. Its observance is that one does not eat [and] look up to the sky. Its result is that one is loved by by the god, and many honourable people love you.

n the eleventh month (May-Juney), on the fifth day of the waxing moon, its deity is the Reverend Leka Jaya. Its observance is that one is sweeping while walking. Its result is that you will be obeyed [by the people], [and] all your speech will be effective.

In the twelfth month (June-August), on the first day of the waxing moon, its deity is the Reverend Pisodharī. Its observance is that one does not sleep with one's wife. Its result is that one will be obeyed by [one's husband] in leading a married life.
These are the calculations of the existence for the months called ‘Flourishing Month’ (Kṛtamasa), which you should hold firmly. It should be remembered, [and] do not forget them.

There is the observance of 'The House of Grandmother' (Saninigraha): one does not put out the fire on Saturday Kalivon. It should be performed for the ten successive Saturday Kalivons. The way to worship is to sweep the shrine [first]. [Then,] Lord Śivāditya should be worshipped to ask permission. The forms of offering in the shrine are [as follows]: anapunar, arih, rәmbaṅ, tambo lagu akah araka, fruits, fragrance flowers, a fragrant cosmetic unguent, fragrant sesame oil, sәḍәṅan ikṣu, light, incense, with fully equipped, devadaru should be polished, [and] seed. All of these [offerings] should be offered to the Lord. The mantra is: “Om̐, salutations to the Goddess, the consort of Vāsudeva. You grant me complete satisfaction. Om̐, obeisances to the glorious spiritual masters. You are the divine offering of the gods; grant great contentment, svāhā!” After finishing it, you should worship using the fragrant [flowers]. The mantra is: “Om̐, hail to the son of the Sun (Sūryaputra). Thus [is how] the observance should be performed. Do not you be careless when [performing] the observance. However, if you are affected by illness or anything else that prevents you from performing the observance, do not firmly decide to perform the observance. Its meaning is: one should take leave from the observance. However, if there will be no obstacle, that is perfectly good, you should firmly decide on performing it. Its result is that one will be reborn as a king in the future; worldly happiness will be obtained; [and] the protection of all other kings; [and] being trusted by all mankind.

This is the quintessence of observance. One who strives for goodness should devote his full attention to it. However, the mind must not be allowed to become impure. This is why you should not think untruthfully while performing the observance, because if the observance is not kept by you, it will cause an obstacle for your body. If the body is to be guarded by you in a pleasant way through the excellent knowledge which is extremely clear and pure, without impurity, without being attached to ear acute pain, and affection (rajah) as well as darkness (tamah). It will cause the great heaven, and also the supreme knowledge. One should know their respective techniques.

There is the observance [that should be performed] on every ‘Umanis day’, one does not eat [the food] that is touched by fire. Its appointed duration is two months. On every Pahiṅ day, one does not eat [the food] that is touched by the fire. Its appointed duration is two months. On every Pon day one does not take a bath [and] touched by the oil, wash one's face, and rince with [water]. Its appointed duration is three months. On every Vage day, one does not sleep in lie down position. Its appointed duration is two years. On every Kalivon day one does not speak. Its appointed duration is two months. Its result is that you will be rewarded by all groups of God no one will follow [your reward], [and] there will be no loss if it is asked [by the people]; your wealth [will be obtained] presently.
This is the sacred teaching on the observances. On the fifth day of the waxing moon, on Kalivon day, one must fast.

Tomorrow on Umanis day, one eats five pieces of Kupat Pandava, [and] its meat is peanuts. Its result is that if one's [desires] have not been obtained in childhood, one will achieve great happiness after one is in old age, as one's great aim.

On Paiṅ day, one eats nine pieces of Kupat Syaṅ Anti, [and] its meat is koma. Its result is that one is guarded by one's parents until one has grandchildren [and] great-grandchild; one will be treated with loving care by one's parents, and one will be desired by one's slaves.

On Pvan (Pon) day, one eats seven pieces of Kupat Sidayu, its meat is salted fish (sudaṅ). Its result is that one will reach a beautiful [appearance] with small, thin, [and] graceful body that is without equal; one will be happy, rich, prosperous, [and] attractive; one will be approached to become the head of co-wife.

On Vage day, one eats four pieces of Kupat Sih Tan Pәgat, its meat is egg. Its result is that one will reach the happy and wealthy; one will be prosperous, powerful, and attractive; one will be obeyed by one's man who will not have the power to leave you; you will be praised by your parents-in law and there is no one will be turned away with a sneer [to you].

On Kalivon day, one eats eight pieces of Aṇḍa Kupat Gәnәp, its meat is rarasmen. Its result is that one will reach the happy, wealthy, and great braveness; one will stand as the Ardhanareśvarī; [and] one will be obeyed [by the people] in speaking.

Tomorrow, on Umanis day, one eats the Aṇḍa Kupat Siddha Luṅguh, its meat is the fish of river, sea-lake, forest-rice field, [and] the meat of [live-stock] in the house. Its result is that one will reach the happy, rich, and great braveness; one will be feared by enemy; one will be treated with loving care by the army and people; one will be approached by the other side army; one will not be blamed by the army, all of them are equally divided without lacking; one will success and effective [in working] without speaking; all the people will losing its lustre; in the audience-hall one will be waited respectfully by the army who is from far away, one baan come from the invisible form every time; if one is a woman she will be served by the co-wife without no one equal, every way will be in good condition; one will be rich in children; one will be feared by the offspring; one will taste the bravery; [all of things] will increase in abundance; being added continuously without decreasing it. All of the dried coconut leaves turn green.

There is the observance of ‘filling the world completely’ (Anuṅku rāt). On Kalivon day, one’s food is smoked. On Umanis day, one’s food is honey. On the Pahiṅ day, one’s food is the wind. On Pvan (Pon) day, one’s food is water. On Vage day, one's food is fire. On the full [and] dark moon one fasts. It should be performed twice. Its result is reaching the utmost observance.

There is the observance of ‘Being Five Days’ (Mañcavāra): On Umanis day, one eats white rice. On Pahiṅ day, one eats the red glutinous rice. On Pon day, one eats yellow rice. On Vage day, one eats black glutinous rice. On Kalivon day, one eats five colours of glutinous rice. In the east direction, one eats white egg. For the south direction one drinks spirituous liquor. For the west direction, one eats a yellow egg. For the north direction, one eats bakatul. In the middle, one eats the pink sarasi. Its result is being happy [and] rich.

There is the observance of ‘Following the Seven Days’ (Saptavāra): On Sunday, one chews betel leaves for five successive Sundays. On Monday, one chews betel leaves for four successive Mondays. On Tuesday, one chews betel leaves for three successive Tuesdays. On Wednesday, one chews betel leaves for seven successive Wednesdays. On Thursday, one chews betel leaves for eight successive Thursdays. On Friday, one chews betel leaves for six successive Fridays. On Saturday, one chews betel leaves for nine successive Saturdays. Its result is being happy [and] rich according to one's wishes.

There is the observance of eating cooked rice placed in a sәlaṅgi for sarahup held in the left hand, with no residue or additions. Its appointed duration is three nights. The Reverend Siddhi Rakṣa descends to perform the observance. His place is in the world. Its result is that you will be descended by happiness while working on goodness; you will not be killed by your child; it will continue straight on until your child and descendants.

There is the observance of eating cooked rice for sarahup held in the left hand, with no residue or additions. Its meat is only uncooked [of food]. Its appointed duration is three nights. It is called ‘working for having a child’ (Kārya Hana Putra). The Reverend Sandi Rasa descends to perform the observance. His place is in the body, [especially in] the secret [part of the body]. Its result is that when you receive your part in performing the goodness, you will have many children, [and] many people will sympathize and love you.

There is the observance of eating cooked rice held in the left hand, including its meat. [Its appointed duration] is according to one’s pleasure. It is called ‘Side of Mind’ (Pakṣa Hiḍәp). Its deity is the Reverend Kuvera. He becomes appearance, becomes skin, [and] becomes eyebrows. Its result is becoming a successful person who has a good heart.
There is the observance of eating cooked rice. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that many people love you. Such observance is called ‘Being Old’ (Anva).

There is the observance of eating only cooked rice. [Its appointed duration] is according to one’s pleasure. The Reverend Puravat descends to perform the observance. Its result is good behaviour, [and] knowing one’s intention The other alternative for this translation is ‘knowing one’s origin’. .

There is the observance of eating white cooked rice on the first of the waxing moon. The Reverend Prasiddha descends to perform the observance. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is being loved by mankind. Such observance is called ‘flowing’.

There is the observance of eating cooked rice that is not yet full-grown. [Its appointed duration] is according to one’s pleasure. Its deity is the Reverend Paravan. Its result is [the ability] to know what one would say.

There is the observance of eating five balls of white cooked rice, five balls of red glutinous rice, five balls of yellow glutinous rice, [tridhātu brata, 5, mañcavāra]. The Reverend Padma Rasa descends to perform the observance. [He becomes] eyes, as well as breath, speech, and mind. Its result is one will be rich [and] any kind of one's intention will not be poor.

There is the observance of eating cooked rice slaṅgi with the pari fish as its meat. Its appointed duration is half of a month. The deity of this observance is the Goddess Ranini Bhaṭārī Uma. Its result is becoming conversant with the right thing, [and] being served by many people.

There is the observance of eating cooked rice slaṅgi. One takes [this observance] for seven full moons. The Reverend Viśeṣa descends to perform the observance. Its result is being rewarded with five supernatural powers. If woman, she will meet [a man with a man with] Viṣṇu’s quality; not taking long [process in learning] and smart; wisdom; being happy and rich in the future.

There is the observance of eating the five colours of cooked rice. [The sugar of] the aren palm is formed into a wheel, [and then] a wick is stuck to it. It should be eaten by you on Kalivon day. This is called 'being the wheel of the world'. The Reverend Śivātma descends to perform the observance. He becomes appearance, becomes life, [and] becomes conduct. Its result is becoming a person who gives life to the world; being happy, rich, and having the power to be the essence of the world, [until] in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of ‘Guarding the Colour’ (Jaga Varṇa): one eats the cooked rice called balañan. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that one is obeyed by mankind; being smart and wisdom, being skillful at playing gamәlan and [singing] the songs; [as well as being] a brave man.

There is the observance if one eats while worshiping the cooked rice. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is being loved by God. Such observance is called ‘Radiance Thought-gem’ (Śrī Cittāmaṇi).

There is the observance of holding cooked rice layered by the wick, if the wick dies you should stop eating. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that every kind of weapon will not be able to penetrate you. The name of such observance is called 'Fasting' (Aṅañcaṅ).

There is the observance of eating [cooked rice] stuck by a round wick. Its deity is the Reverend Anuṅkәbi Rāt. He will become a beautiful [and] handsome appearance. Its result is that one becomes a person who is happy and rich; one will be able to coordinate (lead) the world in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating [cooked rice] which is stuck by a banner bearing [a drawing] in the form of Bhīma. It is called ‘The Reverend of the Jewel Glow’ (Saṅ Hyaṅ Maṇik Teja). The Reverend Paṅirut Jagat descends to perform the observance. He becomes appearance, becomes conduct, [and] becomes glow. Its result is that one will be beautiful [and] followed by weapons, just like flowers accompanied by banners; being powerful and can break down the world in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of ‘Putting the Wick’ (Avr̥tti). If one eats [the food] stuck with a wick. If the wick dies, you should stop eating. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that all your illness will not affect your body.
There is the observance of ‘Being a Glower’ (Aṅәmbaṅ): if one eats with flowers first. Its appointed duration is three years. Its deity is the Lord Īśvara. Its result is that God loves you.

There is the observance of ‘Being a Flower’ (Ṅәmbaṅ): if one does not going away when a guest comes. The Lord Viśeṣa gives the observance. Its result is being rich; occupying a proper position in the village where no one can succeed to compete with [you].

There is the observance of ‘Not Being in Dispute' (Aja Tukar): one eats with the flower of pulava on the side. Its appointed duration is one month. The Lord Guru gives the observance. Its result is having sexual intercourse with a young man; and being loved by a learned man.

There is the observance of eating the flowers avery Umanis. The name of the observance is the ‘Reverend Glowing Jewel’ (Maṇisumila). Its deity is the Reverend Smara. He is serving as the beautiful and glowing appearance of the place where many people assemble in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating [the food] layered with the flower of campaka. The name of the observance is the ‘Reverend of Pudak Gem’ (Saṅ Hyaṅ Maṇik Pudak). The Reverend Vidakā descends to perform the observance. He is serving as the perfect handsome appearance. Its result is being reborn as a nobleman, [particularly] as a person who is happy and rich, [as well as] being wise in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating young and flexible branches (shoots), and these should be used as flowers, two [pieces]. Its deity is the Reverend Maṇik Arṣana. The Lord Bāyu descends to perform the observance. He is serving as appearance, as life, as hair, as lәye, as mind, as neck, as sinduva, [and] as lip. Its result is becoming a happy [and] rich person with a pure mind who wears flowers and fruit in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of balaka as a side dish, all together with a hot condiment (sambal). It is called ‘The Underworld Mantra’ (Mantra Pātāla). The Reverend Basuki descends to perform the observance. He is serving as appearance, as smallness, as sole of the foot, as bon, [and] as kәliṅ. Its result is becoming a happy [and] rich person in freehold, being overcome with longing by the people in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating [the food] layered with seed. It is called ‘The Reverend Hero Flower’ (Saṅ Hyaṅ Vīra Kusuma). The Reverend Jayaniṅ Rāt descends to perform the observance. He is serving as appearance, as face, [and] as skin. Its result is that your appearance is extraordinary [and] powerful. If you become a person, you will be a happy, [and] rich person in the property of the king, gold [and] silver, [as well as] son and daughter in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating [the food] layered with perfume. It is called the ‘Reverend of Prominent Fragrance Flower’ (Saṅ Hyaṅ Mūrva Gaṇḍa Vaṅi). The deity of the observance is the Reverend Maṇik Sumirit. He is serving as appearance, as skin, [and] as smell. Its result is that one becomes a person whose fragrance spreads right through to the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating the flower śrīgaḍiṅ. The name of the observance is the Reverend Jewel Śrīdanti. He is serving as appearance, as gums, [and] as teeth. Its result is being beautiful because of your teeth, happy [and] rich; [the Reverend Vidyaka descends to perform the observance. He is serving as a perfectly handsome, being reborn as nobleman, versed in poetry, [and] wise in the invisible realm.]

There is the observance of eating on a thicket plate. It is called ‘Mindfulness of Flowers’ (Puṣpani Smr̥ti). Its deity is the Lord Smara. He is serving as a basis, and then its result is being loved by father [and] mother.

There is the observance of eating on a leaf plate. It is called ‘Having a Material Form of Breath’ (Amūrti Prāṇa). The Reverend Pagәr Gunuṅ descends to perform the observance. He is serving as the teeth. Its result is longevity, [and] death not by means of a sword.

There is the observance of eating on a leaf plate. Its appointed duration is seven months and seven nights. Its deity is the Lord Mahīśvara. Its result is reaching the [abode] of the Lord Mahīśvata. You will be in one heaven [with Him]. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as chief of language, [and] successful with the king.

There is the observance of eating on the sheath of the spadix of the unexpanded fruit of certain palms. It must be rounded and inhaled. Its result is being rich in dodotDodot: a garment worn around the lower part of the body and siñjaṅ Siñjaṅ: a garment worn by women around the lower part of the body.

There is the observance of eating on a pampat plate. Its number is 73. The young coconut-leaf ballsshould be used. Its result is being happy [and] rich; your body appearance will be handsome and soft; your finger will be pliancy.

There is the observance of 'Omnipresent' (Sarvagata): if one eats with no additional. Its appointed duration is four months [and] four nights. Its result is being smart [and] wisdom; being skilled in playing gamәlan [and] singing; having a speech like a thunderbolt; winning over enemies [and] being obeyed by mankind; bieng happy [and] rich from childhood.

There is the observance of ‘Whatever’ (Asiṅ): [one chews betel leaves once] one eats [the food] while still chewing the betel leaves, and then with no addition. Its appointed duration is one month. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Uma. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Goddess Yana!” [It is recited when applying] make-up. Its result is being happy and rich and completely filling in the royal palace.

There is the observance of not chewing betel, only [eating/chewing ] sәmbuṅ. Its appointed duration is one month. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Kāma Jaya. Its result is that your look (appearance) will be bright [and] fresh completely; your speech will be obeyed by mankind.

There is the observance of ‘Together with Chewing Betel’ (Saṅga Ṅinaṅ). Its appointed duration is one year [and] one month. Its result is that one [will be] in harmony with one’s spouse; [and] being loved by the king. [In applying] make up, the mantra is: ‘Om̐ hail to Braśrīvastu!’.

There is the observance of ‘Loving a Corpse’ (Asihaniṅ Layon): one chews betel without throwing away the quid. The rest of the quid should be gathered [and then] burnt. This is to keep in mind constantly. The mantra is: “Om̐ the Lord is dead, revive to mix with the the cloud, be reborn in every respect extraordinary. It is serving as my food. Sa Ba Ta A I, Hail to Śiva!”
There is the observance of eating half of the areca-palm, accompanied by the pahi fish [as meat]. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Anuṅku Rāt. Its result is that one’s finger will be good.

There is the observance of eating at the side of an incense [and] lamp. It is called the ‘Reverend of the Bright Jewel’ (Saṅ Hyaṅ Maṇik Teja). The Reverend Maṇik Muntab descends to perform the observance. He is serving as an appearance, as bright, [and] as great supernatural power. Its result is that you will become a charismatic person (abhrā murub sumilah), [and] mankind will fear you in an extraordinary way.

There is the observance of ‘Great Lamp’ (Damar Aguṅ): one does not eating until the Reverend Sūrya at sunset. Its appointed duration is one year. [The food] should be eaten is: yuyukan (crab), onion uṅkul, tarasi, sasivi, rarako mali, [and] caṅkuk sarvan vinuṅkul. Its result is being seen by all kinds of difficulty, being free from all kinds of teachings, not having difficulty in learning it, being flowing (smoothing) in [learning] the sacred text, [and] overcoming the difficulty. The deity of the observance is the Lord Śiva.

There is the observance of ‘Time of Approaching Twilight’ (Pasaṅ Saṇḍe): one does not eating until the sun at sunset. Its result is that the mind will be clear; when starting to learn one will be capable (skilled) of it quickly.

There is the observance of not eating on the full moon day of the tenth month (April-May). It should be performed for three successive full moon days in the tenth month (April-May). Its result is that the invisible form of heaven will be found, [and] reborn as a king who is perfectly attractive in the world.

There is the observance of ‘Being always in a Full Moon’ (Mūrṇamasadā): one does not eating on the full moon day until the first day of the waning moon, [and not eating] on the dark moon day until the first day of the waxing moon. Its result is that you will be rich continuously; [and] your goals will be obtained in the world. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Prajuritiṅ Bhūmi.

There is the observance of ‘Feasting’ (Akasukhan). On the full moon day in the seventh month (January-February), one eats, drinks, [and] dances seven times during the day, seven times at night. Its result is being happy [and] rich with children [and] friends, longevity, and being obeyed [as well as] trusted [by the people].

There is the observance [performed] precisely on the third day of the waxing moon, one eats turmeric. It is called ‘always being in the full moon’ (mūrṇamasadā). The deity of the observance is the Reverend Trisandhi. He is the other half of the Lord Mahādeva. He is serving as the appearance, as the skin, and as the wisdom. Its result is not losing something.

On the fourth day of the waxing moon, one eats the black glutinous rice. It is called ‘Enjoying the Accomplishment’ (Amukti Labdha). The deity of the observance is the Reverend Cadu Śakti. He is the other half of the Lord Viṣṇu. He is serving as the appearance, [and] as the hair. Its result is that I have succeeded in giving heaven to my father and mother.

On the fifth day of the waxing moon, [...]. It is called ‘being the five excellent of powerful days’ (amañcavara śakti). The deity of the observance is the Reverend Pañcavāra. He is the other half of the Lord Śiva. He is serving as the appearance, as the mind, [and] as the head. Its result is that I have succeeded in having the wealth without wishing for it.

There is the observance of eating the food (especially edible roots and fruit). One eats the food (especially edible roots and fruit) every on the full moon day [and] dark moon day. The Reverend Patūt Sih descends to perform the observance. Its result is being rewarded with the five supernatural powers. He is serving as the behaviour [to reach] the happiness [and] wealth without taking action.

There is the observance of ‘Following the Full Moon [and] Dark Moon’ (Mūrṇama Tilәm). One fasts from eating food (especially edible roots and fruit). Its result is that your uncle’s debt will be paid. Its result is according to your wish.

There is the observance of eating food (especially edible roots and fruit). It is called ‘leaf’. The Reverend Taruṇa descends to perform the observance. He is serving as an appearance. Its result is that I can successfully become rich in the freehold land.

There is the observance of eating all kinds of fruit: [such as] taro, tubers, or bananas. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is being famous, [and] being desired by women. Such observance is called ‘being the fruit of the tree’ (abhoh kayu).
There is the observance of eating the hanging fruits. It is called ‘Other Side of Leaf’ (Davun Sinabraṅ). Its result is becoming a warrior.

There is the observance of eating all kinds of tubers. [It is performed] according to one’s pleasure. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Viśeṣa. Its result is being happy [and] rich, [and having] a book as a mark of ornament.
There is the observance of eating all kinds of fruit. Its appointed duration is seven nights. Its result is that one is loved by his wife; if one is a woman, she is loved by her husband.

There is the observance of eating and tasting [the food]. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Keḍәp. The place where it will start is in the kitchen. The ingredients should be chewed is growth betel leaf with lime putted on lәmpuyaṅ (Zingiber americana). It is without eating [and] chewing if not biting the lәmpuyaṅ (Zingiber americana). Its result is that one does not be very interested in (crazy about) women, [and] being obeyed towards one’s husband.

There is the observance of eating katambat three grains every kalivon without eating paran-paran. [Its appointed duration] is seven successive kalivon. Its result is that one will be handsome and have smooth hair.

There is the observance of 'Sole of the Earth' (Ambhūmi Lәpa): one eats a soup-like dish eaten with rice putted all on the palm of the hand. Its appointed duration is one month. The Lord Īśvara gives the observance. Its result is that one will be loved by one's wife, obeyed by one's husband, [and] loved by the god.
There is the observance that one should eat the mimba (Azadirachta indica). Its appointed duration is one month. Its result is that one will be beautiful immediately.

There is the observance of ‘Wholly Arrangemen’ (Sarvatatā): one eats the tendril of gaṇḍa rusa kәliṅ and campaka garus. Its deity is the Lord Śambhu. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Guru, and the Lord Śiva.

There is the observance of ‘Eating Seed’ (Vījahāhara): one eats the seeds, the tip of the gaṇḍa rusa, and the tip of thick grass before the others. Its result is that you will become smart, [and] be loved by women.

There is the observance of eating all kinds of tendrils especially those of creepers, the tips of uncultivated grass, the tips of thick grass (alaṅ-alaṅ), lotus, [and] seeds for three pinches. Its appointed duration is seven nights. All of its results are that one’s objective is accomplished. The name of such observance is ‘Doing the First’ (Amūrva).

There is the observance of ‘Being Antavali’ (Ṅantavali): one eats antavali. Its length is one lәṅkat. It should be finished on consecutive seven Saturday Kalivon. [It is completed with] seven peeper seeds, [and] seven ligundi tips. Its result is that all your obstacles will vanish because of that; all your speeches will be obeyed, [and] being obtained now and in the future.

There is the observance of ‘Without Smell/Odorless’ (Nirambə̄): one does not eat any kind of odorless [food]. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Rudra. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a beautiful person, [or] handsome warrior.

There is the observance of eating red glutinous rice seven nights, [and] black [glutinous rice] seven nights. Its meat is all kinds of pure meat (sarvaśuci). It is called the powerful arariṅ. The deity of the observance is Bhagavān Paraśara. Its result is having a handsome relative

There is the observance of eating glutinous rice taṅkәp, one by one on Kalivon, seven [times]. It is added by nutmeg (pala), pepper, [and] benzoin. On Aṅgara Kasih one eats seven handful. The Reverend Asihiṅ Prāṇa descends to perform the observance to be rewarded five supernatural powers. Its result is being happy [and] wealthy, all your desires are fulfilled.
There is the observance of ‘Being Black’ (Anīla): one eats the black glutinous rice. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Viṣṇu. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a minister.
There is the observance of ‘Being Ancient’ (Mūraṇa): one eats the ñahñah and sugar cane. Its appointed duration is three days. Its result is that nothing will obstruct all your purpose.
There is the observance of not eating together with others. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is having great happiness. Such observance is called ‘One Plate’ (Ekapatra).

There is the observance of ‘Unmatched’ (Tan Kapadan): one does not eat together with others. It is accompanied by five silences (pañcamuna). Throughout one's life, one eats the leaves and flowers as a side dish when eating. This is the uppermost among all observances. Its result is that one will be unmatched [and] superior. Such are the deeds of a serious priest.

There is the observance of eating without being together with others. Its appointed duration is four years. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Rūdra. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a noble family, [and] having the famous relative king.

There is the observance of ‘Putting in Order’ (Aṅajum): one eats at the edge. Its appointed duration is one month. The Lord Mahādeva gives the observance. Its result is that one will arrive at one's destination in accordance with one's position, provided one understands what one has heard.

There is the observance of the ‘Rotating Lap’ (Amutәriṅ Paṅkon): one eats on the lap. Its appointed duration is one month. The Lord Mahādeva gives the observance. Its result is being loved by father [and] mother; [and] being loved by male [and] female. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a superior bhujaṅga.
There is the observance of eating when [speaking] softly (in discussion). Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is having a powerful mantra, [and] perfectly beautiful.

There is the observance of ‘Every Man’ (Naṅkәn Nara): one eats while holding coins. Its appointed duration is seven months. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Rudra. Its result is that you will be strong enough [and] not affected by the illness.

There is the observance of being at the side of a coin. Its appointed duration is one month. Lord Indra gives the observance. Its result is being smart and versed in poetry, [and] the sains of architectural (aṣṭa kośala). [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a rich patih.

There is the observance of eating while sticking [a kris] in the belt. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is being rich, successful, [and] effective; having a speech like thunderbolt and being famous.

There is the observance of eating kupat pāṇḍava three pieces. It should be eaten one piece in the morning. It should be eaten in one piece at noon. It should be eaten in one piece at noon. Its result is being guarded by mankind, being worn the sawit by all people; [and] its result will not be obstruct.

There is the observance of eating kupat with all kinds of pure meat. Its appointed duration is three nights. The deity of the observance is the Lord Īśvara. Its result is being skillful at singing, having a good appearance of head, a sweet mouth, and being loved by people.
There is the observance of eating lәpәt. Its appointed duration is half of a month. The deity of the observance is Ranini Kuṇḍaṅ Kasih. Its result is that one will be effortless.

There is the observance of eating rice cones. Its length is one hasta. The meat is empty, [and] it is only salt [and] charcoal. It is called ‘Behaving like Sarasvatī’ (Anarasvatī). The deity of this observance is the Reverend Pitu Tan Palavan. He serves as a smart [person]. Its result is being loved by male and female, being an undiminished successful and rich person, and the woman will fill the world completely.

There is the observance of eating rice cones. Its appointed duration is half a month. If this is not possible, it can be performed for seven days. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Ra Nini Paduka Bhaṭarī. Its result is that one's neck is good.
There is the observance of not speaking the truth. The Lord Rudra gives the observance. Its result is being rich in [a garment] that hangs down.
There is the observance of keeping one’s arms folded over one's chest for the entire day. The Lord Śaṅkara gives the observance. Its result is being loved by people.

There is the observance of walking for one night [and] one day. The Lord Guru gives the observance. Its result is that [...] if something goes wrong, one is reborn as the divine teacher, having many disciples, being handsome in appearance, being seen as very bright, being rich from childhood, [and] being rich flowing continuously.

There is the observance of being concentrated wholly on the mouth for one day and one night while facing the east. The Reverend Anәmu Jagat descends to perform the observance. He is serving as a parent, [and] as deeds of woman. Its result is being rewarded with five supernatural powers, smart, a wise male, being happy [and] rich, now and shortly.

There is the observance of ṅalamuñĕṅ. The Reverend Lәbur Jagat descends to perform the observance. One will be rewarded by the five supernatural powers, for one person who always performs this observance. He is serving as appearance, [and] as deeds. [Its result] is that one will indeed reach goodness; male [and] female will be happy, rich, prosperous, [and] being obeyed [by people].

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like the Demon’s Wheel’ (Ṅālacakra). The Reverend Viśeṣa Riṅ Bhuvana descends to perform the observance. He is offered by five spears three protection for as long as he performs the observance. Its result is being happy [and] rich, smart [and] wise, for both male or female.

There is the observance of the ‘Five Excellences of Power’ (Mañcavaśa giṇa): one does not fight against a woman when talking on every Umanis day. If a woman, she does not speak with men, not chewing betel leaf with lime. If it is only leaf, it can be allowed. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that you will be followed by gold, [and] all of the property presently.

There is the observance of ‘Smooking the Body’ (Kukusaniṅ Śarīra): one does not eat the meat of quadrupeds. Its appointed duration is according to one’s ability to perform the observance. The Reverend Caduśakti descends to perform the observance. He is serving as an appearance, [and] as buttock. [Its result] is that one will be successful in having pearls, many people will sympathize, [and] the companion will love you. This embraces all other observances.
There is the observance of not eating pork. Its deity is the Reverend Manasija. Its appointed duration is seven years. Its result is being free from serious illness, and being loved by the world.
There is the observance of not eating jackal (wild dog). Its result is that your appearance will not be lusterless.
There is the observance of not eating chicken meat. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that one does not meet an enemy.
There is the observance of not eating chicken meat. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is that one will not be together with a co wife and be happy.

There is the observance of ‘Using a Kris’ (Akәrisa): one does not eating before polishing one’s teeth continuously. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Śvari. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is that you will become smart, [and] you have a successful start in gold.

There is the observance of having ḍaḍap (Erythrina indica) at the side. Its appointed duration is three days without eating. Its deity is the Lord Śiva. Its result is reaching the superior heaven; being famous; being born as a famous noble family, and then becoming excellent, and becoming supreme bahudaṇda.

There is the observance of ‘Every Seventh Month’ (Ṅapitu): one fasts every twelfth day of the seventh bright half of the lunar month. Its deity is the Lord Bhīma. The mantra is: Om̐ Bam̐ hail to Bhīma. [I take] leave. Its result is that one will become a brave man [and] trusted by mankind; becoming rich in gold and silver, servants, and many children; all your action will succeed.
There is the observance of ‘Every Thursday’ (Ṅrәspati): its technique is that one fasts every thursday. Its result is that you will become beautiful, and all your activity will be good.
There is the observance of not eating for seven nights. Its result is that you will become a brave man [and] all your activities will be successful.

There is the observance of fasting for one month in the tenth month (April-Mey). Its result is that one will be trusted by mankind; gold and silver will come in abundance; and will be loved by learned men.

There is the observance of not eating anything that breathes when the birthday ritual comes. Its result is that one will obtain the [successful] in leading the married life. Its virtue will not be decreased. Its deity is the Lord Rudra.
There is the observance of not eating anything that breathes, on Pvan day, [and] Kalivon day. Its result is being obeyed by mankind.

There is the observance of ‘Being Brave’ (Amiraṅ): one does not eat any kind of breathing creature (any creature that breathes). Its appointed duration is one year and three months. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Pabyavara. Its result is that all your desires will be found, [and] God loves you.

There is the observance when eating at the side of flower-sign (Puṣpa Liṅga). It is called ‘being the breath-sign’ (aṅliṅga prāṇa). The Reverend Aṅgasti descends to perform the observance. Its result is that you will be obeyed by mankind, and your appearance will flare up (charismatic); you will be a great, significant, powerful [and] warrior. If you are reincarnated as a person, your appearance will shine [and] glow and your appearance will not be defeated. You will have a perfect longevity. You will be an outstanding man.

There is the observance of ‘Using the Fighting-Sign’ (Aṅliṅga Pәraṅ): if one eats at the side of a kris. The deity of the observance is the Lord Rudra. Its result is that many people will defend [and] love you.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like a Taro’ (Āṅubi): one eats and drinks before [eating] other food. After eating, one is not allowed to speak with the person. Its result is being strong, happy and rich, not affected by illness, not straying from the right way, [and] being trusted by mankind.

There is the observance of eating without addition [food], and without drinking water. Its result is that you will be powerful in the invisible realm. Its appointed duration is according to one’s pleasure in performing the observance. Its deity is the Reverend Dura Dasih. When performing the observance, one should not sleep during the day. [Its result] is that your appearance will be bright, your heart will be bright, [and] you will be loved by mankind.

There is the observance of drinking the water of cooked rice. One does not eat the cooked rice in one day, not sleeping day and night. One should sit opposite to what is obtained. [Its result is that] one is reborn as a good person. The mantra is: ‘the empty body contains nothingness; eats the cooked rice on this basis. It is spattered by fresh water!’ [I take leave]. After asking permission, one eats the remaining food. Do not sweep it up!

There is the observance of drinking the water of cooked rice. It is called ‘Entering Five’ (Mañjiṅ Lima). One is allowed to chew betel leaf, and eating the cooked rice while drinking the water, the cooked rice is put on the palm of the hand. It is allowed to drink the water every evening. Its appointed duration for performing the observance is one year if one is able to do so. Its result is vanishing all kinds of pain. Its goal is vanishing the physical body.

There is the observance of not drinking water in the vuku Galuṅan, but you can eat the egg putted in the ground in front dәṅәn, while standing up at the noon. One concentrate to the Lord Mṛtyu. Its result is being dug up and then emerged, completely growing, being a supreme man, being a brave man, being followed by the world, being successful graṅaluṅan.

There is the observance of floating (Aṅambaṅ): one eats the food that has been floated on the water. Its appointed duration is one year. The Lord Viṣṇu gives the observance. Its result is that one is reborn as a relative of the king; being rich in iron; and being a trusted poet, [and] being a warrior.

This is Saṅ Citta Varaṇa's teaching to Saṇ Vala Kula about the origin of all reality. Pay close attention! What is the origin of supreme independence and prosperity, and what are their nature, sign, beginning and ending? These are the questions of Saṇ Vala Kula as he worships his teacher respectfully. "Om̐, holy man, all your questions are intelligent because you are asking truthfully, my son!" Now listen to my words. pūrvam śrī puruṣānte, varānugraha makanya, saṅ rojyam, narāsakane, ayavam vidyām prajayam. Such is the detailed enumeration of the thought. The meaning is [as follows]: pūrva means means origin; Tripuruṣa means the Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśvara; Vara means instruction; Anugraha means welcomed; Manoka means gods; Saroja means aphoristic rule; Nara means human; Sakala means now; Yaśa means meritorious action; [and] Vidyā means scripture; Aprayadha means worship. Its meaning is as follows: the lord performs religious austerity in forests and mountains. The Lord and the Goddess purify themselves by cutting off their strong attachment. [This is why, they] enter [and] living in the forest to perform the religious austerity, yoga, and samadhi. They suffer themselves. [This is] followed by the human now to perform the observance, yoga, samadhi, sacrifice, donation, [and] meritorious actions. The reason for performing the observance is to look (observe) at the organ of perception (ulandriya), [and] hold (control) the organ of perception (The reason for performing these acts is to observe and control the organs of perception). It should be united with three junctures [religious activity] (trisandhyā). If it is compared to the state of highest goal (kaparamartan): yoga serves as the container, samadhi serves as the cover, the observance serves as the presser, donation and meritorious action serves as the guardian, the rule serves as the wanderer, various worships and speech serves as the hedge, welcome serves as the gate, consistency serves as the rulers, the true serves as the door panel, [and] the highest goal serves as defender and key.
These are the behaviours of those who practise prosperity (happiness). Prosperity (happiness) means 'power'. Power means the band of service. The band of service means the richness in family and appearance: being powerful, brave, and free from illness and obstacles; union with the people through the eyes (cakṣyah lavajjanā --> cakṣyuh lavañ jana); strict in religious observance, longevity, youthfulness, a long life. Thus is the result of constantly performing observances. This is the supreme independence [obtained] by a wise man. Such are the words of Saṅ Citta Varaṇa to Saṅ Vala Kula. I worship—what about the supreme independence shortly, my lord? 'I will teach you shortly, you should do my words from now on into the future. By your leave, my lord! Teach me the observance, its detailed enumeration, and its result, my lord! A U MA.

There is the observance of not eating and not sleeping, as is the observance of the Reverend Vәkasiṅ Kavi Siśeṣa. Its result is that one will reach superior heaven, one is reborn as a world-ruler, being perfectly famous, being benevolent in the world, all your intentions will be arrived, accompanied by goodness, being a powerful and extraordinarily brave man.

There is the observance of ‘Following the Sect of Bhairavas’ (Ambhairava Pakṣa): whatever is eaten by one, truly not loving sleep. This is a gift from the Lord Pavaka and gods. Its result is being loved by demons and gandharvas; being reborn as a brave man who is perfectly famous; and being feared by all wild creatures.

There is the observance of not being afraid (revolted) about all kinds of things eaten. It is called modest (simple/unassuming). Its result is that one will be a brave man who is successful and rich from childhood.

There is the observance of ‘imitating charcoal’ (ṅarәṅ): one eats charcoal before other. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Gaṅga. The mantra is: “Om ̐hail to Gaṅga!” Its appointed duration is one month. Its result is not being attracted to the world.
There is the observance of eating the charcoal of rice cones. Its appointed duration is four years. Its result is being obeyed by all people, being loved by mankind, being obeyed by children.
There is the observance of eating once. Its appointed duration is seven months [and] seven nights. Its result is being loved by mankind.

There is the observance of ‘The Sequence of Moral Conduct’ (Niṭikrama): one eats once in one day. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Smara. Its result is that whatever one desires will be found quickly.
There is the observance of eating seven times. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that one will be loved by mankind.
There is the observance of grounding to banish from the world. Its result is being rich in freehold land.
There is the observance of eating on the ground. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is being loved by mankind. This observance is called ‘The Earth’ (Bhūmi).

There is the observance of ‘Following Five Days’ (Mañcavāra): On the Umanis, one eats facing east. On Paiṅ, one eats facing south. On Pvan (Pon), one eats facing west. On Vage, one eats facing north. On Kalivon, one eats facing whichever direction one wishes. All of these are accompanied by side dishes and flowers in colours to match the cooked rice. These colours are five colours, namely white, yellow, red, black, and the five colours in the middle. Its deity is Deva Rata. Its result is reaching the heaven [and] abode of the Lord Śiva. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a world ruler who is matchless (without equal). The mantra is: “Om̐ Om̐ hail to illustrious the Jagat Guru!” [I take] leave.

There is the observance of ‘Following the Inner Part of the Five Days’ (Mañcavāra Dalәm). Its technique is that: one only eats salt, [and then] eats only cooked rice. Its appointed duration is one month and three days. After that, one only drinks water. After that, one only chews betel. Once the appointed duration is finished, one is allowed to eat [again] without falling asleep. Its deity for the observance is the Reverend Vәkasiṅ Anuṅku Rāt. [Its result is that] your happiness will not decrease. [If something] goes wrong, you will reach the heaven of the Lord Dharma. You will be reincarnated as a one who loves eating without working, not being difficult in taking a job, [and] you will be happy without knowing its origin. People, gods, and a bhikṣuka will love you and come to you.
There is the observance of living on trees. Its result is having many children, and whatever you say will be obeyed.
There is the observance of [living] on trees. Its result is having many children, and whatever you say will be obeyed.

There is the observance of ‘Going Through the Forest’ (Aṅalas): one hiding in the forest for one day, without being met by people, especially all kinds of animals, including one's perfume. Its result is that the warrior in the boat, will go up his material on water. The charcoal of the warrior on the ground will put his material on the stone. The Reverend Buddha gives the observance.[Its result is that if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as master of a ship, being rich in irrigated rice fields, and being rich in boats.

There is the observance of eating fruit (especially edible roots and fruit) every dark moon and full moons. It is called ‘Wholly Accomplished’ (Sarvaputus). The Reverend Silih Asih gives the observance. Its result is being guarded by father and mother; being happy and rich because of self effort; and without seeking protection from an old person.

There is the observance of eating bananas without barking. Its appointed duration is three nights. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Murṣita. Its result is being a handsome person. If one is female, one will have an attractive appearance and a kind heart, and will understand the meaning of one’s parents’ advice.

There is the observance of eating the tuhuṅ pitpit before the others. The name of the observance is the Reverend Glitter Jewel (saṅ hyaṅ maṇik muñcar). The Reverend Maṇik Aṅuñci Pәpәt descends to perform the observance. He is serving as appearance, as the body of woman, [and] as the beauty. Its result is that you will be happy and nice; being flooded by a handsome person, prosperous in children and grandchildren in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of ‘Floating the Bean’ (Milir Kacaṅ): Its technique is to fast in one day, [and then] eat in one day. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Prajā Sadā. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Īśvara. [If something] goes wrong, you will be reborn as a happy, rich, and perfectly prominent person. If you are male, you will be reborn into a skilled and benevolent family. One will be rich in coins in the future. Such is the [result] if you are a woman.

There is the observance of eating the essence of safflower (Carthamus tinctorius). It is called the ‘Reverend Jewel King of Paddy’ (Saṅ Hyaṅ Maṇik Pari Rāja). The Reverend Maṇik Teja Bhūmi descends to perform the observance. He is serving as appearance, as blood and flesh, [and] as liver. Its result is happiness, rich, [and] beauty; [like] an unwithered flower, flourishing, [and] bearing fruit in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating a handful of cooked rice. It is called the ‘Reverend Jewel Received’ (Saṅ Hyaṅ Maṇik Tampa). The deity of the observance is Reverend Maṇḍala. He is serving as an appearance, [and] as a kukusan (cone-shaped basket of woven bamboo in which rice is steamed) of the body. Its result is to be filled completely with large and small pieces of gold adorning beautiful finger; being a successful person who is happy [and] rich, without cutting off the accomplishment, and gold as well jewel; you will be accompanied by the world [and] accompanied by recitation of mantras (muttered prayer) in the future.

There is the observance of eating white and yellow cooked rice every Kalivon day, while facing east. It should [be accompanied] by bīra as meat. It is eaten once [a day] for nine successive kalivon days, [or] the best time is nine months, as is its appointed duration. The Lord Śiva is the deity of the observance. He is the other half of the Lord Antadeva. He is serving as appearance, as the whole, [and] as the longevity. If one is a male, he is serving as handsome, as deeds, [and] as charm. If one is female, he is serving as the beauty, as deeds, as mother. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Śiva. [If something] goes wrong, one is reborn as a supreme ruler, priest [or] bhujaṅga both in Śiva or Buddha sect; being completely rich in gold and silver, all kinds of gems, children, slaves, water buffalo-ox, special forest animal, rich in offspring, being guarded by father and mother, and grand father as well as grand mother. The mantra is: 'Om̐ hram̐ hrim̐ hail to the highest form of Śiva Sun' [when applying] make up.

There is the observance of ‘Rulling’ (Amiśeṣa): one eats [the food] without decoration. The cooked rice should be eaten until finished, if one has already married. The mantra is that: the soul should be remembered by the Supreme Lord, he is to be positioned at the vindhu and nadha in the visible and invisible realms. Because of the Supreme Lord Baja, one dies in a standing position, one dies in a sitting position, and one quickly vanishes from sight, having a body without a material body in the visible and invisible realm.

There is the observance of ‘Following All the Conduct of the Lord Gaṇa’ (Saśila Gaṇa). It is called ‘Being the Flowers of the [Lord] Gana (Amuṣpa Gaṇa): if one eats six handfuls of cooked rice in one day. The manner is sitting politely on the ground with the legs crossed as the Gaṇa’s position while eating. Its appointed duration is six months. Its result is reaching the [heaven] of the Lord Guru. [If something] goes wrong, you will be reborn as a viku ijo, who has the supernatural powers of sight that can see distant or hidden things. All your speech will be obeyed.

There is the observance of eating cooked rice held on the left hand, without remaining, without adding, [and] without choosing the meat. It is called ‘Being the Perfect Lotus’ (Apadmayoni). The Reverend Siddhi Narasiṅha will descends to bless the observance. He is serving as appearance, [and] as deeds. Its result is the accomplishment of connecting [with others] through speech; [and] being loved by mankind. The mantra is: “Om̐, Om̐ hail to the cause of spiritual accomplishment!” [It is recited when applying] make up.

There is the observance of ‘the Appearance of Jaṅga’ (Jaṅga Varṇa): one eats only the cooked rice. (by eating only cooked rice). Its appointed duration for repeating the exercise is seven days. Its result is that all your speech is obeyed by mankind; being smart [and] wise; being skilful at playing gamәlan and singing.

There is the observance of ‘Protecting from the Enemy’ (Jaga Śatru). The deity of the observance is the Reverend Saptanala (Saṅ Hyaṅ Saptanala). Its technique is: one can only sleep on the first day of the waxing moon of the two times [of the waxing moon] meeting with the seventh day of the waxing moon after the moon at the set. [After] passing the seventh day of the waxing moon, you can sleepas you wish. Likewise, you can only sleep for half of a lunar month on the waning moon if it has already risen. When passing through this period you can sleep as you wish. Its result is being a rich person, without [anyone] being able to stop your meritorious act in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of ‘Being Glow’ (Mārab) I have conjectured the word mūrāba as mārab, as the former does not appear in the OJED or Balinese dictionaries. I assume that mūraba is a mystical form of mārab, which means ‘to flare, flame, blaze, glow’ (OJED, s.v.). It is also consistent with the technique of performing the observance, whereby the practitioner eats certain types of flowers.
: one should start performing the observance on the fourth day of the waxing moon. One should eat the flower of nāgasāri (Mesua ferrea), pūraṇa (Clitoria ternatea) Nāgasāri: According to the text titled Kavi Jānaki, collected in Unit Lontar, Udayana University. I found the word purāṇa used to designate one plant, namely itil. The text contains: krĕntikā, smaracatrā, wagaprańā, puranā, gamantya ṅa itil (Kavi Jānaki, 16r). In the oral tradition, the word itil refers to the talaṅ flower (Clitoria ternatea).,
[and] kulalaṭa I have not found the specific plant to which kulalaṭa refers. OJED (s.v.) explains that lalaṭa is a particular kind of flower or floral motif. .
It should end on the full moon. Its result is being handsome [or] beautiful without equal. The mantra is: 'Om̐ hail to Smara! [It is recited] when applying make-up.

There is the observanceThis passage does not provide a detailed explanation of the technique for performing the observance. I assume that the word mopavāsa ‘fasting’ is needed here to complete the explanation. The word brata itself also has the meaning of a ‘holy practice’ (fasting, continence, etc.) (OJED, s.v.). [perfomed] on the eleventh day of the waxing moon. It is called ‘beyond the smoke’ (Atikukus). Its result is becoming a brave man, [and] being perfectly prosperous.

There is the observance of eating half cooked-rice
I translate aron-aron as ‘half-cooked rice’ rather than ‘with leaves’ (variant form of aron-ron). I assume the word aron-aron was derived from the words haru or aru. In Old Javanese, haru-daṅ means ‘a pot for half-cooked rice’ and paṅarvan means ‘a pot in which half-cooked rice is stirred before being put back in the kukusan’ (ModJ) (OJED, s.v.).
