In Balinese, the words haru/aru + -an become aruwan/aron (another instance for this sound change is: kalaṅvan → kalaṅon/kalaṅәn, vvaṅ → voṅ, etc. ), meaning ‘half-cooked rice’. ,
[and] burning coconuts. Its appointed duration is fifteen days. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Viśeṣa. Its result is a beautiful head.

There is the observance of eating without using a leaf [as a plate]. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that one's actions are successful. The name of such observance is ‘Record of Victory’ (Jayapattra) OJED (s.v.) defines the term jayapattra as ‘a record of victory (in a lawsuit) given to the victorious party’. In this context, I only use ‘record of victory’ to make the translation jayapattra more precise. .

There is an observance that over powers all [other] observances. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Umapati. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong one will reborn as a world ruler; being a powerful priest who has many disciples; having received fame as a gift.
There is the observance of being like a child who will not keep a secret. Its result is that you are not reincarnated repeatedly. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a king.

There is the observance of putting out the fire, chewing betel for three days, [and] not eating all kinds [of food]. It is finished after three daysOther alternatives for this translation is ‘the food is taken after abstinence for three days’., and should be sprinkled with holy water. Its result is that all of one’s pain vanishes.

There is the observance of consuming sәsәḍĕpSәsәḍep is finely chopped betel etc with dadap leaves, bras and kuñit used as bhasma on the temples, between the eyes, on the head and the shoulder-blades (esp. in certain ceremonies) (OJED s.v.) before the other. Its appointed duration is seven years. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Vastu. Its result is being obeyed by mankind.
There is the observance of eating the salt mix with charcoal as meat. Its result is being obeyed by mankind, being followed by the world, [and] being feared by enemies.

There is the observance of eating the [cooked rice] with four colours. Its appointed duration is five nights. Its result is becoming smart [and] powerful, and then being loved by mankind. You [will become] prominent. The name of such observance is sakabdhu The word sakabdhu does not exist in OJED and Balinese dictionaries. I have not found any interpretations of this word yet.

There is the observance of eating during the day, five [times] The number 5 in the text is not clearly explained. For the time being, this number 5 is interpreted as ‘5 times’. I put it in the brackets. Another possibility is ‘5 handfuls of food per day’. . Its result is that your fingers and skin will be fine.

There is the observance of ‘Following Interval’ (Ṅantāra): one eats in the middle of the day, [and] in the middle of the night. Its appointed duration for repeated exercise is three months. Its result is that all your descendants become powerful, [and experience] great happiness.

There is the observance of eating seven handfuls [of food] in one day. Its appointed duration to perform the observance is seven days. The name of the observance is four (Catur) I have not found yet the releation between the name of this observance catur ‘four’ with the technique to perform the observance and the duration.. Its result For the reason in adding the word pha, in this passage see footnote 3.331. is that you will be reborn as a person with a body unaffected by any type of iron in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating without sitting. The Reverend Hayu gives the observance. The name of the observance is the Reverend of Walking (Saṅ Hyaṅ Laku). He serves as an appearance who is beautifully attractive. Its result
I have added the word pha, meaning ‘its result’ in accordance with the general pattern found in other passages of the Tattva Brata. Pha is typically placed after the mantra portion: ma, om̐ śambhave namaḥ, pamit, pha, mañjanma riṅ kulaputra (3.26); after the duration of the brata: tigaṅ tahun lavasnya, pha, drәman aputra, siṅ prih meṅgal katəkan (3.27); after the technical details of the brata’s performance: hana brata tan pamaṅan ivak bavi, pha, tan kataman deniṅ sarvaviṣya (3.63), after the name of the brata: saṅ hyaṅ kr̥ta bhuvana hyaṅniṅ brata, pha, etc. (3.87).
is being happy in your journey; the ash of your trace is followed by attendants; you will be successful with happiness and wealth; you will enjoy the palace in the future.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Open Hall’ (Maṇḍapa): one eats in the lap using the leaves as a base. The Reverend Sūkṣma gives the observance. Its result is that all your deeds are fit (completely right), [and] your relationship with your spouse is not cut off. Its appointed duration is one month. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the [Reverend] Sūkṣma!” [I take] leave.

There is the observance of not eating all kinds of breathing beings every Pon Pon is the third day in the five-day cycle (pañcavāra) of the Old Javanese/Balinese calendar system. and Kalivon Kalivon is the fifth day in the five-day cycle (pañcavāra) of the Old Javanese/Balinese calendar system.day. Its result is being obeyed by mankind.

There is the observance of eating while looking in the mirror every full moon day. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is being reborn as a rich senior customary village head (kabayan buyut)
The word kabayan means ‘old; an elder, chief, leader’ (OJED, s.v.), while buyut means ‘great-grandfather, great-grandchild; elder’ (OJED, s.v.). In the Balinese context, the word kabayan refers to a ‘customary village head’ (KBI, 2016: 96). For this reason, in this context, I translate kabayan buyut as ‘senior customary village head’. .

This is the sacred text on the hair (Aji Rambut): one eats the black cooked rice every fourth day of the bright half of the lunar month. The mantra is: “I am performing the sacred teaching of the hair that is not red, not transparent, not white. May my hair be black just like a crow: long, soft I have emended the word alambas to alәmәs. The Balinese word alambas meaning ‘long’ (KBI, 2016: 540) is already expressed by the word adavā ‘long’ (OJED, s.v.) in the previous word in this sentence. The word alәmәs meaning ‘pliant, lithe, lissom, supple, slender, and soft’ (OJED, s.v.) is a more suitable choice in this context as the main topic is about the hair. , [and] thick. It is obtained presently. I am performing the sacred teaching of hair, which is good presently. Surely, I am performing the sacred teaching of hair. Om̐ Sa Ba Ta A I! Hail to Śiva!”
There is the observance of being silent in worship. Its result is that you will be loved by God.

There is the observance of being silent when defecating, urinating, taking a bath, applying oil, wearing undergarments, [and] walking. Its appointed duration is seven months. Lord Śiva gives the observance. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one will be rich in property, rich in offspring, and be obeyed [by people], [as well as] being reborn as a minister.

In 1722 Śaka (1800 AD), on Thursday Kalivon, Vāra MarakihMarakih is the name of the 16th vuku (OJED, s.v.), on the first day of the bright lunar fortnight in the month Asuji (September-October). The unit is two. The tens are two. That is the time when it is completely written.This manuscript was completed at the end of the 18th century.
